sentences.zh: __FORCETOC__自周衰，禮樂壞于戰國而廢絕于秦。

translations.literal: __FORCETOC__From the Zhou decline, rites and music were ruined in the Warring States and abolished in Qin.
translations.idiomatic: __FORCETOC__When the Zhou declined, rites and music were spoiled in the Warring States and cut off entirely under Qin.

sentences.zh: 漢興，六經在者，皆錯亂、散亡、雜偽，而諸儒方共補緝，以意解詁，未得其真，而讖緯之書出以亂經矣。

translations.literal: When Han arose, of the Six Classics that survived, all were disordered, scattered, lost, and mixed with forgeries; the scholars were just then jointly patching and binding them, glossing by whim, and had not attained the truth, when apocryphal and weft-text books appeared to confuse the classics.
translations.idiomatic: When the Han rose, the surviving Six Classics were all disordered, scattered, adulterated, and lost; scholars were still piecing them together and glossing by guesswork without recovering the true text, when apocryphal and weft-text books appeared to confuse the canon.

sentences.zh: 自鄭玄之徒，號稱大儒，皆主其說，學者由此牽惑沒溺，而時君不能斷決，以為有其舉之，莫可廢也。

translations.literal: From Zheng Xuan and his followers, styled great Confucians, all upheld those doctrines; scholars were thereby led astray and drowned in them, while the rulers of the age could not decide, thinking that since there were those who upheld them, none could abolish them.
translations.idiomatic: From Zheng Xuan onward, men hailed as great Confucians all championed those doctrines; scholars were drawn under and drowned in them, while contemporary rulers could not settle the matter, supposing that because someone upheld a practice, it could not be abolished.

sentences.zh: 由是郊、丘、明堂之論，至於紛然而莫知所止。

translations.literal: Hence discussions of suburban, mound, and Bright Hall rites became so tangled that no one knew where to stop.
translations.idiomatic: Hence debate over suburban altars, mound sacrifices, and the Bright Hall grew so tangled that no one knew where to stop.

sentences.zh: 禮曰：「以禋祀祀昊天上帝。

translations.literal: The Rites say: "With smoke-offering sacrifice one sacrifices to August Heaven the Supreme Lord."
translations.idiomatic: The Rites say: "With smoke-offering sacrifice one sacrifices to August Heaven the Supreme Lord."

sentences.zh: 」此天也，玄以為天皇大帝者，北辰耀魄寶也。

translations.literal: " This is Heaven; Xuan took it to be the Heavenly Emperor the Great Emperor—Polaris, the Shining Soul Treasure Star.
translations.idiomatic: " This is Heaven itself; Zheng Xuan identified it as the Heavenly Emperor the Great Emperor—Polaris, the Shining Soul Treasure Star.

sentences.zh: 又曰：「兆五帝於四郊。

translations.literal: It also says: "Establish the Five Emperors at the four suburbs."
translations.idiomatic: It also says: "Establish the Five Emperors at the four suburbs."

sentences.zh: 」此五行精氣之神也，玄以為青帝靈威仰、赤帝赤熛怒、黃帝含樞紐、白帝白招拒、黑帝汁光紀者，五天也。

translations.literal: " These are the spirits of the five phases' vital essences; Xuan took them to be the Blue Emperor Spiritual Majesty Uplifted, the Scarlet Emperor Scarlet Blaze Wrath, the Yellow Emperor Holding the Pivot, the White Emperor White Summons Rejected, and the Black Emperor Juice Light Record—the Five Heavens.
translations.idiomatic: " These are the spirits of the five phases' vital essences; Zheng Xuan identified them as the Blue Emperor Spiritual Majesty Uplifted, the Scarlet Emperor Scarlet Blaze Wrath, the Yellow Emperor Holding the Pivot, the White Emperor White Summons Rejected, and the Black Emperor Juice Light Record—the Five Heavens.

sentences.zh: 由是有六天之說，後世莫能廢焉。

translations.literal: Hence arose the doctrine of Six Heavens, which later ages could not abolish.
translations.idiomatic: Thus arose the doctrine of the Six Heavens, which no later age could abolish.

sentences.zh: 唐初貞觀禮，冬至祀昊天上帝于圓丘，正月辛日祀感生帝靈威仰于南郊以祈穀，而孟夏雩于南郊，季秋大享于明堂，皆祀五天帝。

translations.literal: In early Tang, the Zhenguan Rites prescribed that at the winter solstice August Heaven the Supreme Lord was sacrificed at the Round Mound; on the xin day of the first month the Life-Giving Emperor Spiritual Majesty Uplifted was sacrificed at the southern suburb to pray for grain; in mid-summer there was rain-prayer at the southern suburb; in late autumn the great offering was at the Bright Hall—all sacrificing to the Five Heavenly Emperors.
translations.idiomatic: Under early Tang's Zhenguan Rites, the winter solstice sacrifice to August Heaven the Supreme Lord was held at the Round Mound; on the first month's xin day the Life-Giving Emperor Spiritual Majesty Uplifted was sacrificed at the southern suburb to pray for grain; mid-summer rain-prayer and late-autumn great offering at the Bright Hall all honored the Five Heavenly Emperors.

sentences.zh: 至高宗時，禮官以謂太史圓丘圖，昊天上帝在壇上，而耀魄寶在壇第一等，則昊天上帝非耀魄寶可知，而祠令及顯慶禮猶著六天之說。

translations.literal: By Gaozong's time, ritual officers said that in the Grand Astrologer's Round Mound diagram August Heaven the Supreme Lord was on the altar summit while the Shining Soul Treasure was on the altar's first tier—so August Heaven the Supreme Lord was clearly not the Shining Soul Treasure—yet the Sacrificial Code and Xianqing Rites still recorded the Six Heavens doctrine.
translations.idiomatic: By Gaozong's reign, ritual officers noted that on the Grand Astrologer's Round Mound diagram August Heaven the Supreme Lord stood atop the altar while the Shining Soul Treasure occupied the first tier—proving they were not the same—yet the Sacrificial Code and Xianqing Rites still enshrined the Six Heavens doctrine.

sentences.zh: 顯慶二年，禮部尚書許敬宗與禮官等議曰：「六天出於緯書，而南郊、圓丘一也，玄以為二物；

translations.literal: In the second year of Xianqing, Minister of Rites Xu Jingzong and the ritual officers deliberated: "The Six Heavens issue from weft-text books; the southern suburb and Round Mound are one, yet Xuan took them as two things;
translations.idiomatic: In Xianqing year 2, Xu Jingzong, Minister of Rites, and the ritual officers argued: "The Six Heavens derive from weft-text books; the southern suburb and Round Mound are one rite, yet Zheng Xuan treated them as two;

sentences.zh: 郊及明堂本以祭天，而玄皆以為祭太微五帝。

translations.literal: suburban and Bright Hall rites were originally to sacrifice to Heaven, yet Xuan took them all as sacrifices to the Supreme Palace Five Emperors.
translations.idiomatic: suburban and Bright Hall rites were meant to honor Heaven, yet Zheng Xuan held them all to be sacrifices to the Supreme Palace Five Emperors.

sentences.zh: 傳曰：『凡祀，啟蟄而郊，郊而後耕。

translations.literal: The Commentary says: 'For all sacrifices, when hibernating insects stir, suburban sacrifice; only after suburban sacrifice does plowing follow.'
translations.idiomatic: The Commentary says: 'For every sacrifice, when hibernating insects stir, perform suburban sacrifice; only after suburban sacrifice does plowing follow.'

sentences.zh: 』故『郊祀后稷，以祈農事。

translations.literal: ' Hence 'suburban sacrifice to Hou Ji to pray for agricultural affairs.'
translations.idiomatic: ' Hence 'suburban sacrifice to Hou Ji to pray for the harvest.'

sentences.zh: 』而玄謂周祭感帝靈威仰，配以后稷，因而祈穀。

translations.literal: ' Yet Xuan said Zhou sacrificed to the Life-Giving Emperor Spiritual Majesty Uplifted, with Hou Ji as associate, and thereby prayed for grain.
translations.idiomatic: ' Yet Zheng Xuan claimed Zhou sacrificed to the Life-Giving Emperor Spiritual Majesty Uplifted with Hou Ji as associate, and thereby prayed for grain.

sentences.zh: 皆繆論也。

translations.literal: All are erroneous doctrines.
translations.idiomatic: All of this is mistaken doctrine.

sentences.zh: 」由是盡黜玄說，而南郊祈穀、孟夏雩、明堂大享皆祭昊天上帝。

translations.literal: " Thereupon Xuan's doctrines were wholly rejected, and southern-suburb grain-prayer, mid-summer rain-prayer, and Bright Hall great offering all sacrificed to August Heaven the Supreme Lord.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon Zheng Xuan's doctrines were wholly rejected, and southern-suburb grain-prayer, mid-summer rain-prayer, and Bright Hall great offering all honored August Heaven the Supreme Lord.

sentences.zh: 乾封元年，詔祈穀復祀感帝。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianfeng, an edict restored sacrifice to the Life-Giving Emperor for grain-prayer.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianfeng year 1, an edict restored sacrifice to the Life-Giving Emperor for grain-prayer.

sentences.zh: 二年，又詔明堂兼祀昊天上帝及五帝。

translations.literal: In the second year, another edict ordered the Bright Hall jointly to sacrifice to August Heaven the Supreme Lord and the Five Emperors.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, another edict ordered the Bright Hall to honor both August Heaven the Supreme Lord and the Five Emperors.

sentences.zh: 開元中，起居舍人王仲丘議曰：「按貞觀禮祈穀祀感帝，而顯慶禮祀昊天上帝。

translations.literal: In the Kaiyuan era, Attendant Gentleman Wang Zhongqiu deliberated: "According to the Zhenguan Rites, grain-prayer sacrifices to the Life-Giving Emperor, while the Xianqing Rites sacrifice to August Heaven the Supreme Lord.
translations.idiomatic: In the Kaiyuan era, Attendant Gentleman Wang Zhongqiu argued: "The Zhenguan Rites sacrifice to the Life-Giving Emperor for grain-prayer, while the Xianqing Rites sacrifice to August Heaven the Supreme Lord.

sentences.zh: 傳曰：『郊而後耕。

translations.literal: The Commentary says: 'After suburban sacrifice comes plowing.'
translations.idiomatic: The Commentary says: 'After suburban sacrifice comes plowing.'

sentences.zh: 』詩曰：『噫嘻春夏，祈穀于上帝。

translations.literal: ' The Odes say: 'Ah, spring and summer—grain-prayer to the Supreme Lord.'
translations.idiomatic: ' The Odes say: 'Ah, spring and summer—grain-prayer to the Supreme Lord.'

sentences.zh: 』禮記亦曰：『上辛祈穀于上帝。

translations.literal: ' The Record of Rites also says: 'On the upper xin day, grain-prayer to the Supreme Lord.'
translations.idiomatic: ' The Record of Rites also says: 'On the upper xin day, grain-prayer to the Supreme Lord.'

sentences.zh: 』而鄭玄乃云：『天之五帝迭王，王者之興必感其一，因別祭尊之。

translations.literal: ' Yet Zheng Xuan said: 'Heaven's Five Emperors take turns as kings; when a king rises he must be moved by one of them, and therefore sacrifices separately to honor him.
translations.idiomatic: ' Yet Zheng Xuan said: 'Heaven's Five Emperors reign in turn; when a king rises he is moved by one of them, and therefore sacrifices separately to honor that deity.

sentences.zh: 故夏正之月，祭其所生之帝於南郊，以其祖配之。

translations.literal: Hence in the first month of summer one sacrifices to the emperor from whom one was born at the southern suburb, with one's ancestor as associate.
translations.idiomatic: Hence in the first summer month one sacrifices at the southern suburb to the emperor from whom one's house was born, with one's ancestor as associate.

sentences.zh: 故周祭靈威仰，以后稷配，因以祈穀。

translations.literal: Hence Zhou sacrifices to Spiritual Majesty Uplifted with Hou Ji as associate, and thereby prays for grain.
translations.idiomatic: Hence Zhou sacrifices to Spiritual Majesty Uplifted with Hou Ji as associate, and thereby prays for grain.

sentences.zh: 』然則祈穀非祭之本意，乃因后稷為配爾，此非祈穀之本義也。

translations.literal: ' Yet grain-prayer is not the original intent of sacrifice; it is only because Hou Ji serves as associate—this is not the original meaning of grain-prayer.
translations.idiomatic: ' Yet grain-prayer is not sacrifice's original purpose; it arose only because Hou Ji serves as associate—this is not grain-prayer's true meaning.

sentences.zh: 夫祈穀，本以祭天也，然五帝者五行之精，所以生九穀也，宜於祈穀祭昊天而兼祭五帝。

translations.literal: Grain-prayer is fundamentally to sacrifice to Heaven; yet the Five Emperors are the essences of the five phases whereby the nine grains are produced—at grain-prayer one should sacrifice to August Heaven and also sacrifice to the Five Emperors.
translations.idiomatic: Grain-prayer is fundamentally sacrifice to Heaven; yet the Five Emperors are the essences of the five phases that produce the nine grains—grain-prayer should honor August Heaven and include the Five Emperors.

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「月令，大雩、大享帝，皆盛祭也。

translations.literal: " He also said: "In the Monthly Ordinances, great rain-prayer and great offering to the emperors are all grand sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: " He also said: "In the Monthly Ordinances, great rain-prayer and great offering to the emperors are both grand sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 而孟夏雩、季秋大享，貞觀禮皆祭五方帝，而顯慶禮皆祭昊天上帝，宜兼用之以合大雩、大享之義。

translations.literal: Yet for mid-summer rain-prayer and late-autumn great offering, the Zhenguan Rites all sacrifice to the Five Directional Emperors while the Xianqing Rites all sacrifice to August Heaven the Supreme Lord—both should be used together to accord with the meaning of great rain-prayer and great offering.
translations.idiomatic: For mid-summer rain-prayer and late-autumn great offering, the Zhenguan Rites honor the Five Directional Emperors while the Xianqing Rites honor August Heaven the Supreme Lord—both should be combined to satisfy the meaning of great rain-prayer and great offering.

sentences.zh: 」既而蕭嵩等撰定開元禮，雖未能合古，而天神之位別矣。

translations.literal: " Thereafter Xiao Song and others compiled the Kaiyuan Rites; though they could not accord with antiquity, the ranks of heavenly spirits were now distinct.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereafter Xiao Song and others compiled the Kaiyuan Rites; though they could not match antiquity, the ranks of heavenly spirits were at last distinguished.

sentences.zh: 其配神之主，武德中，冬至及孟夏雩祭皇地祇于方丘、神州地祇於北郊，以景帝配；

translations.literal: As for associated spirits: in the Wude era, at the winter solstice and mid-summer rain-prayer the August Earth Lord was sacrificed at the Square Mound and the Spirit of the Land of the Divine Province at the northern suburb, with Emperor Jing as associate;
translations.idiomatic: As for associated spirits: under Wude, at the winter solstice and mid-summer rain-prayer the August Earth Lord was honored at the Square Mound and the Spirit of the Land of the Divine Province at the northern suburb, with Emperor Jing as associate;

sentences.zh: 而上辛祈穀祀感帝于南郊，季秋祀五方天帝於明堂，以元帝配。

translations.literal: on the upper xin day grain-prayer sacrificed to the Life-Giving Emperor at the southern suburb; in late autumn the Five Directional Heavenly Emperors were sacrificed at the Bright Hall, with Emperor Yuan as associate.
translations.idiomatic: on the upper xin day grain-prayer honored the Life-Giving Emperor at the southern suburb; in late autumn the Five Directional Heavenly Emperors were honored at the Bright Hall, with Emperor Yuan as associate.

sentences.zh: 貞觀初，圓丘、明堂、北郊以高祖配，而元帝惟配感帝。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenguan, the Round Mound, Bright Hall, and northern suburb had Gaozu as associate, while Emperor Yuan was associate only for the Life-Giving Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Zhenguan, the Round Mound, Bright Hall, and northern suburb had Gaozu as associate, while Emperor Yuan was associate only for the Life-Giving Emperor.

sentences.zh: 高宗永徽二年，以太宗配祀明堂，而有司乃以高祖配五天帝，太宗配五人帝。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yonghui, Gaozong had Taizong as associate at the Bright Hall, but the responsible officials made Gaozu associate for the Five Heavenly Emperors and Taizong associate for the Five Human Emperors.
translations.idiomatic: In Yonghui year 2, Taizong was made associate at the Bright Hall, but the responsible officials paired Gaozu with the Five Heavenly Emperors and Taizong with the Five Human Emperors.

sentences.zh: 太尉長孫无忌等與禮官議，以謂：「自三代以來，歷漢、魏、晉、宋，無父子同配於明堂者。

translations.literal: Grand Preceptor Zhangsun Wuji and the ritual officers deliberated, saying: "From the Three Dynasties onward, through Han, Wei, Jin, and Song, there was never father and son jointly associated at the Bright Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Preceptor Zhangsun Wuji and the ritual officers argued: "From the Three Dynasties through Han, Wei, Jin, and Song, father and son were never jointly associated at the Bright Hall.

sentences.zh: 祭法曰：『周人禘嚳而郊稷，祖文王而宗武王。

translations.literal: The Canon of Sacrifices says: 'Zhou people performed di to Ku and suburban sacrifice to Ji; they took Wen as zu and Wu as zong.'
translations.idiomatic: The Canon of Sacrifices says: 'Zhou performed di to Ku and suburban sacrifice to Ji; they took Wen as zu and Wu as zong.'

sentences.zh: 』鄭玄以祖宗合為一祭，謂祭五帝、五神于明堂，以文、武共配。

translations.literal: ' Zheng Xuan merged zu and zong into one sacrifice, holding that the Five Emperors and Five Spirits were sacrificed at the Bright Hall with Wen and Wu jointly as associates.
translations.idiomatic: ' Zheng Xuan merged zu and zong into one rite, holding that the Five Emperors and Five Spirits were sacrificed at the Bright Hall with Wen and Wu jointly as associates.

sentences.zh: 而王肅駁曰：『古者祖功宗德，自是不毀之名，非謂配食於明堂。

translations.literal: Wang Su rebutted: 'In antiquity zu honored merit and zong honored virtue—those were titles never to be destroyed, not meaning joint feasting at the Bright Hall.'
translations.idiomatic: Wang Su rebutted: 'In antiquity zu honored merit and zong honored virtue—titles never to be destroyed, not joint feasting at the Bright Hall.'

sentences.zh: 』春秋傳曰：『禘、郊、祖、宗、報，五者國之典祀也。

translations.literal: ' The Spring and Autumn Commentary says: 'Di, suburban, zu, zong, and bao—these five are the state's canonical sacrifices.'
translations.idiomatic: ' The Zuo Commentary says: 'Di, suburban, zu, zong, and bao—these five are the state's canonical sacrifices.'

sentences.zh: 』以此知祖、宗非一祭。

translations.literal: ' From this one knows zu and zong are not one sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: ' From this one knows zu and zong are not a single rite.

sentences.zh: 」於是以高祖配于圓丘，太宗配于明堂。

translations.literal: " Thereupon Gaozu was associated at the Round Mound and Taizong at the Bright Hall.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon Gaozu was associated at the Round Mound and Taizong at the Bright Hall.

sentences.zh: 乾封二年，詔圓丘、五方、明堂、感帝、神州皆以高祖、太宗並配。

translations.literal: In the second year of Qianfeng, an edict ordered the Round Mound, Five Directions, Bright Hall, Life-Giving Emperor, and Spirit of the Land all to have Gaozu and Taizong jointly as associates.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianfeng year 2, an edict ordered the Round Mound, Five Directions, Bright Hall, Life-Giving Emperor, and Spirit of the Land all to have Gaozu and Taizong jointly as associates.

sentences.zh: 則天垂拱元年，詔有司議，而成均助教孔玄義、太子右諭德沈伯儀、鳳閣舍人元萬頃范履冰議皆不同，而卒用萬頃、履冰之說。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chuigong, Empress Wu ordered deliberation; Academician Kong Xuanyi, Right Mentor of the Heir Shen Boyi, and Phoenix Pavilion Attendants Yuan Wanqing and Fan Lubing all differed, but in the end Wanqing and Lubing's view prevailed.
translations.idiomatic: In Chuigong year 1, Empress Wu ordered deliberation; Kong Xuanyi, Shen Boyi, Yuan Wanqing, and Fan Lubing all disagreed, but Wanqing and Lubing's view prevailed in the end.

sentences.zh: 由是郊、丘諸祠，常以高祖、太宗、高宗並配。

translations.literal: Henceforth at suburban and mound sacrifices Gaozu, Taizong, and Gaozong were regularly jointly associated.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth at suburban and mound rites Gaozu, Taizong, and Gaozong were regularly associated together.

sentences.zh: 開元十一年，親享圓丘，中書令張說、衞尉少卿韋縚為禮儀使，乃以高祖配，而罷三祖並配。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Kaiyuan, when the emperor personally enjoyed the Round Mound, Chief Minister Zhang Yue and Chamberlain for the Imperial Clan Wei Chao served as ritual commissioners; Gaozu alone was associated and the three-ancestor joint association was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyuan year 11, when the emperor personally offered at the Round Mound, Zhang Yue and Wei Chao served as ritual commissioners; only Gaozu was associated and joint association of three ancestors was abolished.

sentences.zh: 至二十年，蕭嵩等定禮，而祖宗之配定矣。

translations.literal: By the twentieth year, when Xiao Song and others fixed the rites, association of ancestors was settled.
translations.idiomatic: By year 20, when Xiao Song and others fixed the rites, ancestral association was settled.

sentences.zh: 寶應元年，太常卿杜鴻漸、禮儀使判官薛頎歸崇敬等言：「禘者，冬至祭天於圓丘，周人配以遠祖。

translations.literal: In the first year of Baoying, Director of the Imperial Sacrifices Du Hongjian, Ritual Commissioner Assessor Xue Qi, Gui Jingchong, and others said: "Di is winter-solstice sacrifice to Heaven at the Round Mound; Zhou people associated their remote ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: In Baoying year 1, Du Hongjian, Xue Qi, Gui Jingchong, and others said: "Di is winter-solstice sacrifice to Heaven at the Round Mound; Zhou people associated their remote ancestor.

sentences.zh: 唐高祖非始封之君，不得為太祖以配天地。

translations.literal: Tang Gaozu was not the lord of the original enfeoffment and could not serve as Grand Ancestor to associate with Heaven and Earth.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Gaozu was not the lord of the original enfeoffment and could not serve as Grand Ancestor associated with Heaven and Earth.

sentences.zh: 而太祖景皇帝受封于唐，即殷之契、周之后稷也，請以太祖郊配天地。

translations.literal: Yet Grand Ancestor Emperor Jing received enfeoffment in Tang—he is Tang's Qi and Zhou's Hou Ji—please associate the Grand Ancestor at suburban sacrifice with Heaven and Earth.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Grand Ancestor Emperor Jing received enfeoffment in Tang—Tang's Qi and Zhou's Hou Ji—let the Grand Ancestor associate at suburban sacrifice with Heaven and Earth.

sentences.zh: 」諫議大夫黎幹以謂：「禘者，宗廟之事，非祭天，而太祖非受命之君，不宜作配。

translations.literal: " Remonstrance Councillor Li Gan held that "di is an affair of the ancestral temple, not sacrifice to Heaven, and the Grand Ancestor was not a lord who received the Mandate—he should not serve as associate."
translations.idiomatic: " Remonstrance Councillor Li Gan held that "di concerns the ancestral temple, not Heaven; the Grand Ancestor did not receive the Mandate and should not serve as associate."

sentences.zh: 」為十詰十難以非之。

translations.literal: He composed ten questions and ten objections to refute it.
translations.idiomatic: He composed ten questions and ten rebuttals against the proposal.

sentences.zh: 書奏，不報。

translations.literal: The memorial was submitted but received no response.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was submitted but received no reply.

sentences.zh: 乃罷高祖，以景皇帝配。

translations.literal: Gaozu was removed and Emperor Jing was associated.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu was removed and Emperor Jing was made associate.

sentences.zh: 明年旱，言事者以為高祖不得配之過也。

translations.literal: The next year there was drought; memorialists held it the fault of Gaozu not being associated.
translations.idiomatic: The next year brought drought; memorialists blamed Gaozu's removal from association.

sentences.zh: 代宗疑之，詔羣臣議。

translations.literal: Daizong was doubtful and ordered the ministers to deliberate.
translations.idiomatic: Daizong was uncertain and ordered the ministers to deliberate.

sentences.zh: 太常博士獨孤及議曰：「受命於神宗，禹也，而夏后氏祖顓頊而郊鯀；

translations.literal: Court Academician Dugu Ji deliberated: "Receiving the Mandate from the Divine Ancestor—Yu; yet the Xia honored Zhuanxu at the temple and sacrificed to Gun at the suburb;
translations.idiomatic: Court Academician Dugu Ji argued: "Receiving the Mandate from the Divine Ancestor was Yu; yet Xia honored Zhuanxu in the temple and sacrificed to Gun at the suburb;

sentences.zh: 纘禹黜夏，湯也，而殷人郊冥而祖契；

translations.literal: continuing Yu and deposing Xia—Tang; yet the Yin people sacrificed at the suburb to Ming and took Qi as zu;
translations.idiomatic: continuing Yu and deposing Xia was Tang; yet the Shang sacrificed at the suburb to Ming and took Qi as zu;

sentences.zh: 革命作周，武王也，而周人郊稷而祖文王。

translations.literal: the revolution that made Zhou—King Wu; yet Zhou people sacrificed at the suburb to Ji and took King Wen as zu.
translations.idiomatic: the revolution that made Zhou was King Wu; yet Zhou sacrificed at the suburb to Ji and took King Wen as zu.

sentences.zh: 太祖景皇帝始封于唐，天所命也。

translations.literal: Grand Ancestor Emperor Jing first received enfeoffment in Tang—Heaven's command.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Ancestor Emperor Jing first received enfeoffment in Tang—Heaven's command.

sentences.zh: 」由是配享不易。

translations.literal: " Hence associated worship was not changed.
translations.idiomatic: " Hence associated worship was not changed.

sentences.zh: 嗚呼，禮之失也，豈獨緯書之罪哉！

translations.literal: Alas, the loss of ritual—is it only the fault of weft-text books!
translations.idiomatic: Alas—the loss of ritual is not the fault of weft-text books alone!

sentences.zh: 在於學者好為曲說，而人君一切臨時申其私意，以增多為盡禮，而不知煩數之為黷也。

translations.literal: It lies in scholars' fondness for forced interpretations, and rulers' wholesale improvisation to suit private intent, taking multiplication as exhaustive ritual without knowing that prolixity becomes impiety.
translations.idiomatic: It lies in scholars' fondness for forced interpretations and rulers' wholesale improvisation to suit private whim, taking multiplication for exhaustive ritual without seeing that prolixity becomes impiety.

sentences.zh: 古者祭天於圓丘，在國之南，祭地於澤中之方丘，在國之北，所以順陰陽，因高下，而事天地以其類也。

translations.literal: In antiquity Heaven was sacrificed at the Round Mound in the state's south; Earth at the Square Mound in the marsh within the state in the north—thereby complying with yin and yang, following high and low, and serving Heaven and Earth each with its kind.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity Heaven was sacrificed at the Round Mound south of the capital; Earth at the Square Mound in the northern marsh—complying with yin and yang, following terrain, and serving Heaven and Earth each with its proper kind.

sentences.zh: 其方位既別，而其燎壇、瘞坎、樂舞變數亦皆不同，而後世有合祭之文。

translations.literal: Their positions being distinct, the fire-altars, burial pits, music, and dances also all differed—yet later ages had texts for combined sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Their positions being distinct, fire-altars, burial pits, music, and dances all differed—yet later ages produced texts for combined sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 則天天冊萬歲元年，親享南郊，始合祭天地。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tiansui Wansui of the Zhou dynasty, the emperor personally enjoyed the southern suburb and first combined sacrifice to Heaven and Earth.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhou Tiansui Wansui year 1, the emperor personally offered at the southern suburb and first combined sacrifice to Heaven and Earth.

sentences.zh: 睿宗即位，將有事於南郊，諫議大夫賈曾議曰：「祭法，有虞氏禘黃帝而郊嚳，夏后氏禘黃帝而郊鯀。

translations.literal: When Ruizong took the throne and was about to perform rites at the southern suburb, Remonstrance Councillor Jia Zeng deliberated: "The Canon of Sacrifices: You of Yu performed di to the Yellow Emperor and suburban sacrifice to Ku; Xia performed di to the Yellow Emperor and suburban sacrifice to Gun.
translations.idiomatic: When Ruizong was about to perform rites at the southern suburb, Remonstrance Councillor Jia Zeng argued: "The Canon of Sacrifices: You of Yu performed di to the Yellow Emperor and suburban sacrifice to Ku; Xia performed di to the Yellow Emperor and suburban sacrifice to Gun.

sentences.zh: 郊之與廟，皆有禘也。

translations.literal: Suburb and temple each have di.
translations.idiomatic: Suburb and temple each have di.

sentences.zh: 禘於廟，則祖宗合食於太祖；

translations.literal: Di at the temple: ancestors jointly feast at the Grand Ancestor;
translations.idiomatic: Di at the temple: ancestors jointly feast at the Grand Ancestor;

sentences.zh: 禘於郊，則地祇羣望皆合於圓丘，以始祖配享。

translations.literal: di at the suburb: the Earth Lord and host of territorial spirits all combine at the Round Mound, with the founding ancestor as associate.
translations.idiomatic: di at the suburb: the Earth Lord and territorial spirits all combine at the Round Mound, with the founding ancestor as associate.

sentences.zh: 蓋有事之大祭，非常祀也。

translations.literal: These are great sacrifices on special occasions, not regular worship.
translations.idiomatic: These are great sacrifices for special occasions, not regular worship.

sentences.zh: 三輔故事：『祭于圓丘，上帝、后土位皆南面。

translations.literal: Records of the Three Metropolises: 'Sacrifice at the Round Mound—the Supreme Lord and Earth Mother both face south.'
translations.idiomatic: Records of the Three Metropolises: 'Sacrifice at the Round Mound—the Supreme Lord and Earth Mother both face south.'

sentences.zh: 』則漢嘗合祭矣。

translations.literal: ' Then Han once combined sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: ' So Han had already combined sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 」國子祭酒褚無量、司業郭山惲等皆以曾言為然。

translations.literal: " Director of the National University Chu Wuliang, Vice Director Guo Shanyun, and others all approved Jia Zeng's words.
translations.idiomatic: " National University Director Chu Wuliang, Vice Director Guo Shanyun, and others all approved Jia Zeng's argument.

sentences.zh: 是時睿宗將祭地於北郊，故曾之議寢。

translations.literal: At that time Ruizong was about to sacrifice to Earth at the northern suburb, so Jia Zeng's proposal was set aside.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Ruizong was about to sacrifice to Earth at the northern suburb, so Jia Zeng's proposal was set aside.

sentences.zh: 玄宗既已定開元禮，天寶元年，遂合祭天地于南郊。

translations.literal: After Xuanzong had fixed the Kaiyuan Rites, in the first year of Tianbao he combined sacrifice to Heaven and Earth at the southern suburb.
translations.idiomatic: After Xuanzong fixed the Kaiyuan Rites, in Tianbao year 1 he combined sacrifice to Heaven and Earth at the southern suburb.

sentences.zh: 是時，神仙道家之說興，陳王府參軍田同秀言：「玄元皇帝降丹鳳門。

translations.literal: At that time the doctrines of immortals and Daoists flourished; Staff Officer Tian Tongxiu of the Prince of Chen's household said: "The August Ancestor of the Mysterious Origin descended at Danfeng Gate."
translations.idiomatic: At that time immortalist and Daoist doctrines flourished; Staff Officer Tian Tongxiu of the Prince of Chen's household reported: "The August Ancestor of the Mysterious Origin descended at Danfeng Gate."

sentences.zh: 」乃建玄元廟。

translations.literal: " A temple to the Mysterious Origin was then built.
translations.idiomatic: " A temple to the Mysterious Origin was then built.

sentences.zh: 二月辛卯，親享玄元皇帝廟；

translations.literal: On the xinmao day of the second month, the emperor personally enjoyed the temple of the August Ancestor of the Mysterious Origin;
translations.idiomatic: On the second month's xinmao day, the emperor personally offered at the temple of the August Ancestor of the Mysterious Origin;

sentences.zh: 甲午，親享太廟；

translations.literal: on jiawu, personally enjoyed the Grand Temple;
translations.idiomatic: on jiawu, personally enjoyed the Grand Temple;

sentences.zh: 丙申，有事于南郊。

translations.literal: on bingshen, performed rites at the southern suburb.
translations.idiomatic: on bingshen, performed rites at the southern suburb.

sentences.zh: 其後遂以為故事，終唐之世，莫能改也。

translations.literal: Thereafter this became precedent; through the Tang no one could change it.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter this became precedent; through the Tang no one could change it.

sentences.zh: 為禮可不慎哉！

translations.literal: In ritual, can one not be cautious!
translations.idiomatic: In ritual—can one not be cautious!

sentences.zh: 夫男女之不相褻於內外也，況郊廟乎？

translations.literal: That men and women do not mingle within and without—how much more at suburban altars and temples?
translations.idiomatic: Men and women do not mingle within and without—how much more at suburban altars and temples?

sentences.zh: 中宗時，將享南郊，國子祭酒祝欽明言皇后當助祭，太常博士唐紹、蔣欽緒以為不可，左僕射韋巨源獨以欽明說為是。

translations.literal: In Zhongzong's time, when about to enjoy the southern suburb, National University Director Zhu Qinming said the empress should assist in sacrifice; Court Academicians Tang Shao and Jiang Qinxu held this impossible; Left Vice Director Wei Juyuan alone approved Zhu Qinming.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhongzong, when about to offer at the southern suburb, Zhu Qinming said the empress should assist; Tang Shao and Jiang Qinxu objected; Left Vice Director Wei Juyuan alone approved Zhu Qinming.

sentences.zh: 於是以皇后為亞獻，補大臣李嶠等女為齋娘，以執籩豆焉。

translations.literal: The empress was therefore made secondary presenter; daughters of ministers including Li Qiao were appointed fasting maidens to hold the baskets and stands.
translations.idiomatic: The empress was made secondary presenter; ministers' daughters including Li Qiao's were appointed fasting maidens to hold baskets and stands.

sentences.zh: 至德宗貞元六年，又以皇太子為亞獻，親王為終獻。

translations.literal: By Dezong's Zhenyuan sixth year, the heir apparent was again made secondary presenter and imperial princes final presenter.
translations.idiomatic: By Dezong's Zhenyuan year 6, the heir apparent was again secondary presenter and imperial princes final presenter.

sentences.zh: 孝經曰：「宗祀文王於明堂，以配上帝。

translations.literal: The Classic of Filial Piety says: "Perform zong sacrifice to King Wen at the Bright Hall to associate with the Supreme Lord."
translations.idiomatic: The Classic of Filial Piety says: "Perform zong sacrifice to King Wen at the Bright Hall to associate with the Supreme Lord."

sentences.zh: 」而三代有其名而無其制度，故自漢以來，諸儒之論不一，至於莫知所從，則一切臨時增損，而不能合古。

translations.literal: " Yet the Three Dynasties had the name without the institution; from Han onward the scholars' discussions differed until none knew which to follow—everything was improvised by addition and subtraction, unable to accord with antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: " The Three Dynasties had the name without the institution; from Han onward scholars disagreed until none knew which view to follow—everything was improvised by addition and subtraction, unable to match antiquity.

sentences.zh: 然推其本旨，要於布政交神於王者尊嚴之居而已，其制作何必與古同！

translations.literal: Yet pushing to the root intent, it comes down to dispensing government and communing with spirits in the ruler's seat of dignity—why must the construction match antiquity!
translations.idiomatic: Yet at root it comes down to dispensing government and communing with spirits in the ruler's seat of dignity—why must construction match antiquity!

sentences.zh: 然為之者至無所據依，乃引天地、四時、風氣、乾坤、五行、數象之類以為倣像，而眾說亦不克成。

translations.literal: Yet those who undertook it had nothing to rely on and cited Heaven and Earth, four seasons, winds, qian and kun, five phases, numbers, and images as models—and the many theories still could not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Yet builders had nothing to rely on and cited Heaven and Earth, seasons, winds, qian and kun, five phases, numbers, and images as models—and the many theories still could not agree.

sentences.zh: 隋無明堂，而季秋大享，常寓雩壇；

translations.literal: Sui had no Bright Hall; the late-autumn great offering was regularly lodged at the rain-prayer altar;
translations.idiomatic: Sui had no Bright Hall; the late-autumn great offering was regularly held at the rain-prayer altar;

sentences.zh: 唐高祖、太宗時，寓於圓丘。

translations.literal: under Gaozu and Taizong it was lodged at the Round Mound.
translations.idiomatic: under Gaozu and Taizong it was lodged at the Round Mound.

sentences.zh: 貞觀中，禮部尚書豆盧寬、國子助教劉伯莊議：「從崑崙道上層以祭天，下層以布政。

translations.literal: In Zhenguan, Minister of Rites Dou Lu Kuan and Academician Liu Bozhuang deliberated: "Following the Kunlun path, the upper level to sacrifice to Heaven, the lower to dispense government."
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenguan, Dou Lu Kuan and Liu Bozhuang argued: "Following the Kunlun path, sacrifice to Heaven on the upper level and dispense government below."

sentences.zh: 」而太子中允孔穎達以為非。

translations.literal: " Yet Palace Attendant Kong Yingda held this wrong.
translations.idiomatic: " Yet Palace Attendant Kong Yingda rejected this.

sentences.zh: 侍中魏徵以謂：「五室重屋，上圓下方，上以祭天，下以布政。

translations.literal: Attendant-in-Chief Wei Zheng held: "Five chambers in a double-eaved hall, round above and square below—above to sacrifice to Heaven, below to dispense government.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zheng argued: "Five chambers in a double-eaved hall, round above and square below—above to sacrifice to Heaven, below to dispense government.

sentences.zh: 自前世儒者所言雖異，而以為如此者多同。

translations.literal: Though what earlier scholars said differed, most who held it thus agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Though earlier scholars differed, most who held this view agreed.

sentences.zh: 至於高下廣狹丈尺之制，可以因事制宜也。

translations.literal: As for regulations of height, breadth, and dimensions in feet and inches, one may adapt to circumstances.
translations.idiomatic: As for height, breadth, and dimensions in feet and inches, one may adapt to circumstances.

sentences.zh: 」祕書監顏師古曰：「周書敍明堂有應門、雉門之制，以此知為王者之常居爾。

translations.literal: " Director of the Palace Library Yan Shigu said: "The Zhou Documents describe the Bright Hall with regulations for the outer and inner gates—from this one knows it was the king's regular residence.
translations.idiomatic: " Palace Library Director Yan Shigu said: "The Zhou Documents describe the Bright Hall with outer and inner gate regulations—from this one knows it was the king's regular residence.

sentences.zh: 其青陽、總章、玄堂、太廟、左右个，皆路寢之名也。

translations.literal: Its Green Yang, Total Manifestation, Mysterious Hall, Grand Temple, and left and right niches are all names of the inner chambers.
translations.idiomatic: Green Yang, Total Manifestation, Mysterious Hall, Grand Temple, and the left and right niches are all names of the inner chambers.

sentences.zh: 文王居明堂之篇，帶弓䪅，禮高禖，九門磔禳，國有酒以合三族，推其事皆與月令合，則皆在路寢也。

translations.literal: The passage on King Wen dwelling in the Bright Hall—girding bow and quiver, rites to the High Matron, exorcism at the nine gates, state wine to unite the three clans—when one traces the affairs all accord with the Monthly Ordinances; then all were in the inner chambers.
translations.idiomatic: The passage on King Wen in the Bright Hall—girding bow and quiver, rites to the High Matron, exorcism at the nine gates, state wine to unite the three clans—traced one by one, all match the Monthly Ordinances; all were in the inner chambers.

sentences.zh: 大戴禮曰在近郊，又曰文王之廟也，此奚足以取信哉？

translations.literal: The Greater Dai Rites says near the outer suburb, and also says King Wen's temple—how can this suffice for belief?
translations.idiomatic: The Greater Dai Rites says near the outer suburb and also calls it King Wen's temple—how can this be credited?

sentences.zh: 且門有臯、庫，豈得施於郊野，謂宜近在宮中。

translations.literal: Moreover gates have watch and store towers—how could they be set in suburban wilds? It should be near within the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover gates have watch and store towers—how could they stand in suburban wilds? It should lie near within the palace.

sentences.zh: 」徵及師古等皆當世名儒，其論止於如此。

translations.literal: " Wei and Shigu were famous Confucians of the age, yet their discussions went no further than this.
translations.idiomatic: " Wei Zheng and Yan Shigu were famous Confucians of their day, yet their discussions went no further than this.

sentences.zh: 高宗時改元總章，分萬年置明堂縣，示欲必立之。

translations.literal: In Gaozong's time the reign title was changed to Zongzhang; Wannian was split off to establish Bright Hall County, showing intent certainly to build it.
translations.idiomatic: Under Gaozong the reign title was changed to Zongzhang; Wannian was split to establish Bright Hall County, signaling intent to build it.

sentences.zh: 而議者益紛然，或以為五室，或以為九室，而高宗依兩議，以帟幕為之，與公卿臨觀，而議益不一。

translations.literal: Deliberators grew more tangled—some held five chambers, some nine; Gaozong followed both views and made it with tent curtains, viewing with dukes and ministers, yet debate grew more divided.
translations.idiomatic: Debate grew more tangled—some wanted five chambers, some nine; Gaozong followed both and built it with tent curtains for ministers to inspect, yet opinions only diverged further.

sentences.zh: 乃下詔率意班其制度。

translations.literal: An edict was then issued arbitrarily promulgating its design.
translations.idiomatic: An edict was then issued arbitrarily promulgating its design.

sentences.zh: 至取象黃琮，上設鴟尾，其言益不經，而明堂亦不能立。

translations.literal: When it came to modeling yellow jade disks and setting owl-tails atop, the talk grew more absurd—and the Bright Hall still could not be established.
translations.idiomatic: When it came to modeling yellow jade disks and setting owl-tails atop, the talk grew more absurd—and the Bright Hall still could not stand.

sentences.zh: 至則天始毀東都乾元殿，以其地立明堂，其制淫侈，無復可觀，皆不足記。

translations.literal: Only under Empress Wu was the eastern capital's Qianyuan Hall destroyed and the Bright Hall built on its site; the design was extravagantly excessive, nothing left worth viewing—all unworthy of record.
translations.idiomatic: Only under Empress Wu was the eastern capital's Qianyuan Hall torn down and the Bright Hall built on its site; the design was extravagantly excessive, nothing worth viewing—unworthy of record.

sentences.zh: 其後火焚之，既而又復立；

translations.literal: Later it burned; then it was rebuilt again;
translations.idiomatic: Later it burned; then it was rebuilt;

sentences.zh: 開元五年，復以為乾元殿而不毀。

translations.literal: in the fifth year of Kaiyuan it was restored as Qianyuan Hall without destruction.
translations.idiomatic: in Kaiyuan year 5 it was restored as Qianyuan Hall without being torn down.

sentences.zh: 初，則天以木為瓦，夾紵漆之。

translations.literal: At first Wu Zetian used wood for tiles, sandwiching ramie and lacquering them.
translations.idiomatic: At first Wu Zetian used wood for tiles, sandwiching ramie and lacquering them.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，玄宗遣將作大匠康𧦬素毀之。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year, Xuanzong sent Master of Works Kang Su to destroy it.
translations.idiomatic: In year 25, Xuanzong sent Master of Works Kang Su to destroy it.

sentences.zh: 𧦬素以為勞人，乃去其上層，易以真瓦。

translations.literal: Kang Su thought it wasted labor and removed only the upper story, replacing it with true tiles.
translations.idiomatic: Kang Su thought it wasted labor, removed only the upper story, and replaced it with real tiles.

sentences.zh: 而迄唐之世，季秋大享，皆寓圓丘。

translations.literal: Yet through the Tang, the late-autumn great offering was always lodged at the Round Mound.
translations.idiomatic: Yet through the Tang, the late-autumn great offering was always lodged at the Round Mound.

sentences.zh: 書曰：「七世之廟，可以觀德。

translations.literal: The Documents say: "A temple of seven generations can display virtue."
translations.idiomatic: The Documents say: "A temple of seven generations can display virtue."

sentences.zh: 」而禮家之說，世數不同。

translations.literal: " Yet ritualists' explanations of the number of generations differ.
translations.idiomatic: " Yet ritualists disagree on the number of generations.

sentences.zh: 然自禮記王制、祭法、禮器，大儒荀卿、劉歆、班固、王肅之徒，以為七廟者多。

translations.literal: Yet from the Wang Zhi, Canon of Sacrifices, and Rites Implements of the Record of Rites, and great Confucians Xun Qing, Liu Xin, Ban Gu, Wang Su, and the like, most held seven temples.
translations.idiomatic: From the Wang Zhi, Canon of Sacrifices, and Rites Implements, and from Xunzi, Liu Xin, Ban Gu, Wang Su, and the like, most held for seven temples.

sentences.zh: 蓋自漢、魏以來，創業之君特起，其上世微，又無功德以備祖宗，故其初皆不能立七廟。

translations.literal: From Han and Wei onward, founding lords rose exceptionally; their upper generations were obscure and lacked merit to complete the ancestors—hence at first none could establish seven temples.
translations.idiomatic: From Han and Wei onward, founding rulers rose from nothing; their forebears were obscure and lacked merit to fill the ancestral line—hence at first none could establish seven temples.

sentences.zh: 唐武德元年，始立四廟，曰宣簡公、懿王、景皇帝、元皇帝。

translations.literal: In the first year of Wude, four temples were first established: Duke Xuanjian, King Yi, Emperor Jing, and Emperor Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: In Wude year 1, four temples were first established: Duke Xuanjian, King Yi, Emperor Jing, and Emperor Yuan.

sentences.zh: 貞觀九年，高祖崩，太宗詔有司定議。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Zhenguan, Gaozu died; Taizong ordered the responsible offices to fix deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenguan year 9, Gaozu died; Taizong ordered deliberation.

sentences.zh: 諫議大夫朱子奢請立七廟，虛太祖之室以待。

translations.literal: Remonstrance Councillor Zhu Zishe requested seven temples, leaving the Grand Ancestor's chamber vacant to await.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrance Councillor Zhu Zishe requested seven temples, leaving the Grand Ancestor's chamber vacant.

sentences.zh: 於是尚書八座議：「禮曰：『天子，三昭三穆，與太祖之廟而七。

translations.literal: The Eight Ministers of the Secretariat then deliberated: "The Rites say: 'The Son of Heaven—three zhao and three mu, with the Grand Ancestor's temple makes seven.'
translations.idiomatic: The Eight Ministers deliberated: "The Rites say: 'The Son of Heaven—three zhao and three mu, with the Grand Ancestor's temple makes seven.'"

sentences.zh: 』晉、宋、齊、梁皆立親廟六，此故事也。

translations.literal: ' Jin, Song, Qi, and Liang all established six intimate temples—this is precedent."
translations.idiomatic: ' Jin, Song, Qi, and Liang all established six intimate temples—this is precedent."

sentences.zh: 」制曰：「可。

translations.literal: The decree said: "Approved."
translations.idiomatic: The decree said: "Approved."

sentences.zh: 」於是祔弘農府君及高祖為六室。

translations.literal: Thereupon Lord of Hongnong and Gaozu were enshrined as six chambers.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Lord of Hongnong and Gaozu were enshrined as six chambers.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，太宗崩，弘農府君以世遠毀，藏夾室，遂祔太宗：及高宗崩，宣皇帝遷于夾室，而祔高宗。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year Taizong died; Lord of Hongnong was destroyed for remoteness in generations and stored in the side chamber, and Taizong was enshrined; when Gaozong died, Emperor Xuan was moved to the side chamber and Gaozong was enshrined.
translations.idiomatic: In year 23 Taizong died; Lord of Hongnong was destroyed for remoteness and stored in the side chamber, and Taizong was enshrined; when Gaozong died, Emperor Xuan moved to the side chamber and Gaozong was enshrined.

sentences.zh: 皆為六室。

translations.literal: All were six chambers.
translations.idiomatic: All remained six chambers.

sentences.zh: 武氏亂敗，中宗神龍元年，已復京太廟，又立太廟于東都。

translations.literal: When the Wu clan's disorder collapsed, in Zhongzong's first Shenlong year the capital Grand Temple was restored and a Grand Temple was established at the eastern capital.
translations.idiomatic: When the Wu disorder collapsed, in Zhongzong's Shenlong year 1 the capital Grand Temple was restored and a Grand Temple was established at the eastern capital.

sentences.zh: 議立始祖為七廟，而議者欲以涼武昭王為始祖。

translations.literal: Deliberation arose to establish the founding ancestor for seven temples; deliberators wished to make Prince Zhaowang of Liang the founding ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: Debate arose to establish a founding ancestor for seven temples; some wished to make Prince Zhaowang of Liang the founding ancestor.

sentences.zh: 太常博士張齊賢議以為不可，因曰：「古者有天下者事七世，而始封之君謂之太祖。

translations.literal: Court Academician Zhang Qixian deliberated that this was impossible, saying: "In antiquity those who possessed the realm served seven generations; the lord of the original enfeoffment is called the Grand Ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: Court Academician Zhang Qixian argued this impossible, saying: "In antiquity rulers of the realm served seven generations; the lord of the original enfeoffment is the Grand Ancestor.

sentences.zh: 太祖之廟，百世不遷。

translations.literal: The Grand Ancestor's temple is never moved for a hundred generations.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Ancestor's temple is never moved for a hundred generations.

sentences.zh: 至祫祭，則毀廟皆以昭穆合食于太祖。

translations.literal: At di and xia sacrifices, destroyed temples all jointly feast at the Grand Ancestor by zhao and mu.
translations.idiomatic: At di and xia sacrifices, destroyed temples all jointly feast at the Grand Ancestor by zhao and mu.

sentences.zh: 商祖玄王，周祖后稷，其世數遠，而遷廟之主皆出太祖後，故合食之序，尊卑不差。

translations.literal: Shang's ancestor the Dark King and Zhou's ancestor Hou Ji—their generations are remote, and moved temples' lords all issue after the Grand Ancestor; hence the order of joint feasting does not err in honor and baseness.
translations.idiomatic: Shang's Dark King and Zhou's Hou Ji stand generations remote; moved lords all descend from the Grand Ancestor, so joint feasting preserves proper rank.

sentences.zh: 漢以高皇帝為太祖，而太上皇不在合食之列，為其尊於太祖也。

translations.literal: Han took Emperor Gao as Grand Ancestor, yet the Grand Emperor Supreme was not in the joint-feasting series, being honored above the Grand Ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: Han took Emperor Gao as Grand Ancestor, yet the Grand Emperor Supreme was excluded from joint feasting as senior to the Grand Ancestor.

sentences.zh: 魏以武帝為太祖，晉以宣帝為太祖，武、宣而上，廟室皆不合食于祫，至隋亦然。

translations.literal: Wei took Emperor Wu as Grand Ancestor, Jin Emperor Xuan as Grand Ancestor—above Wu and Xuan, temple chambers were not jointly feasted at xia, and so through Sui.
translations.idiomatic: Wei took Emperor Wu as Grand Ancestor, Jin Emperor Xuan as Grand Ancestor—above them, temple chambers did not join xia feasting, as through Sui.

sentences.zh: 唐受天命，景皇帝始封之君，太祖也，以其世近，而在三昭三穆之內，而光皇帝以上，皆以屬尊不列合食。

translations.literal: Tang received Heaven's Mandate; Emperor Jing was the lord of original enfeoffment, the Grand Ancestor; his generation being near, he was within the three zhao and three mu, while above Emperor Guang all were excluded from joint feasting by senior rank.
translations.idiomatic: Tang received the Mandate; Emperor Jing, lord of original enfeoffment, was Grand Ancestor; his generation being near, he fell within three zhao and three mu, while above Emperor Guang all were excluded by senior rank.

sentences.zh: 今宜以景皇帝為太祖，復祔宣皇帝為七室，而太祖以上四室皆不合食于祫。

translations.literal: Now Emperor Jing should be Grand Ancestor, Emperor Xuan re-enshrined for seven chambers, and the four chambers above the Grand Ancestor should not jointly feast at xia."
translations.idiomatic: Now Emperor Jing should be Grand Ancestor, Emperor Xuan re-enshrined for seven chambers, and the four chambers above the Grand Ancestor should not join xia feasting."

sentences.zh: 」博士劉承慶、尹知章議曰：「三昭三穆與太祖為七廟者，禮也。

translations.literal: Academicians Liu Chengqing and Yin Zhizhang deliberated: "Three zhao and three mu with the Grand Ancestor for seven temples is ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Chengqing and Yin Zhizhang argued: "Three zhao and three mu with the Grand Ancestor for seven temples is ritual law.

sentences.zh: 而王迹有淺深，太祖有遠近，太祖以功建，昭穆以親崇。

translations.literal: Yet royal traces have shallow and deep stages; the Grand Ancestor has near and far; the Grand Ancestor is established by merit, zhao and mu by intimacy.
translations.idiomatic: Royal traces have shallow and deep stages; the Grand Ancestor has near and far; the Grand Ancestor is established by merit, zhao and mu by intimacy.

sentences.zh: 有功者不遷，親盡者則毀。

translations.literal: Those with merit are not moved; when intimacy is exhausted they are destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Those with merit are not moved; when intimacy is exhausted they are destroyed.

sentences.zh: 今以太祖近而廟數不備，乃欲於昭穆之外，遠立當遷之主以足七廟，而乖迭毀之義，不可。

translations.literal: Now the Grand Ancestor is near yet temple numbers are incomplete—wishing beyond zhao and mu to establish remotely lords due for removal to complete seven temples violates the meaning of successive destruction—impossible."
translations.idiomatic: Now the Grand Ancestor is near yet temple numbers are incomplete—wishing beyond zhao and mu to install lords due for removal to complete seven temples violates successive destruction—this cannot stand."

sentences.zh: 」天子下其議大臣，禮部尚書祝欽明兩用其言，於是以景皇帝為始祖，而不祔宣皇帝。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven sent the deliberation down to great ministers; Minister of Rites Zhu Qinming used both views; thereupon Emperor Jing was made founding ancestor without enshrining Emperor Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor referred the debate to ministers; Zhu Qinming used both views; Emperor Jing was made founding ancestor without enshrining Emperor Xuan.

sentences.zh: 已而以孝敬皇帝為義宗，祔于廟，由是為七室，而京太廟亦七室。

translations.literal: Thereafter Emperor Xiaojing was made the Righteous Ancestor and enshrined in the temple—thus seven chambers, and the capital Grand Temple also seven chambers.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter Emperor Xiaojing was made Righteous Ancestor and enshrined—seven chambers in the capital Grand Temple.

sentences.zh: 中宗崩，中書令姚元之、吏部尚書宋璟以為「義宗，追尊之帝，不宜列昭穆，而其葬在洛州，請立別廟于東都，而有司時享，其京廟神主藏于夾室」。

translations.literal: When Zhongzong died, Chief Minister Yao Yuanzhi and Minister of Personnel Song Jing held that "the Righteous Ancestor, a posthumously honored emperor, should not stand in zhao and mu; his burial is in Luozhou—request a separate temple at the eastern capital with regular seasonal offerings, and store his capital temple tablets in the side chamber."
translations.idiomatic: When Zhongzong died, Yao Yuanzhi and Song Jing held that "the Righteous Ancestor, posthumously honored, should not stand in zhao and mu; buried in Luozhou—establish a separate eastern-capital temple with seasonal offerings and store his capital tablets in the side chamber."

sentences.zh: 由是祔中宗，而光皇帝不遷，遂為七室矣。

translations.literal: Thereupon Zhongzong was enshrined; Emperor Guang was not moved—thus seven chambers.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongzong was enshrined; Emperor Guang was not moved—seven chambers.

sentences.zh: 睿宗崩，博士陳貞節、蘇獻等議曰：「古者兄弟不相為後，殷之盤庚，不序於陽甲；

translations.literal: When Ruizong died, Academicians Chen Zhenjie and Su Xian deliberated: "In antiquity brothers did not succeed one another; Yin Pan Geng is not sequenced after Yang Jia;
translations.idiomatic: When Ruizong died, Chen Zhenjie and Su Xian argued: "In antiquity brothers did not succeed one another; Yin Pan Geng is not sequenced after Yang Jia;"

sentences.zh: 漢之光武，不嗣於孝成；

translations.literal: Han Guangwu did not succeed Xiaocheng;
translations.idiomatic: Han Guangwu did not succeed Xiaocheng;

sentences.zh: 而晉懷帝亦繼世祖而不繼惠帝。

translations.literal: yet Jin Emperor Huai succeeded Shizu and not Emperor Hui.
translations.idiomatic: yet Jin Emperor Huai succeeded Shizu, not Emperor Hui.

sentences.zh: 蓋兄弟相代，昭穆位同，至其當遷，不可兼毀二廟。

translations.literal: When brothers alternate, zhao and mu positions coincide; when removal is due, two temples cannot both be destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: When brothers alternate, zhao and mu coincide; when removal is due, two temples cannot both be destroyed.

sentences.zh: 荀卿子曰：『有天下者事七世。

translations.literal: Master Xun said: 'Those who possess the realm serve seven generations.'
translations.idiomatic: Xunzi said: 'Those who possess the realm serve seven generations.'"

sentences.zh: 』謂從禰以上也。

translations.literal: ' Meaning from the father upward.
translations.idiomatic: ' Meaning from the father upward.

sentences.zh: 若傍容兄弟，上毀祖考，則天子有不得事七世者矣。

translations.literal: If one sideways accommodates brothers and destroys ancestors above, then the Son of Heaven cannot serve seven generations.
translations.idiomatic: If one sideways accommodates brothers and destroys ancestors above, the Son of Heaven cannot serve seven generations.

sentences.zh: 孝和皇帝有中興之功而無後，宜如殷之陽甲，出為別廟，祔睿宗以繼高宗。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaohe had restoration merit but no heir; he should be like Yin Yang Jia, set out as a separate temple, and Ruizong enshrined to continue Gaozong."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaohe had restoration merit but no heir; like Yin Yang Jia he should have a separate temple, with Ruizong enshrined to continue Gaozong."

sentences.zh: 」於是立中宗廟于太廟之西。

translations.literal: A temple to Zhongzong was then established west of the Grand Temple.
translations.idiomatic: A temple to Zhongzong was established west of the Grand Temple.

sentences.zh: 開元十年，詔宣皇帝復祔于正室，謚為獻祖，幷謚光皇帝為懿祖。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Kaiyuan, an edict re-enshrined Emperor Xuan in the main chamber with posthumous title Xianzu, and posthumously titled Emperor Guang Yizu.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyuan year 10, an edict re-enshrined Emperor Xuan in the main chamber as Xianzu and posthumously titled Emperor Guang Yizu.

sentences.zh: 又以中宗還祔太廟，於是太廟為九室。

translations.literal: Zhongzong was also returned to the Grand Temple—thus the Grand Temple had nine chambers.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongzong was returned to the Grand Temple—the Grand Temple had nine chambers.

sentences.zh: 將親祔之，而遇雨不克行，乃命有司行事。

translations.literal: When about to enshrine in person, rain prevented it; the responsible offices were ordered to perform the rites.
translations.idiomatic: When about to enshrine in person, rain prevented it; the responsible offices performed the rites.

sentences.zh: 寶應二年，祧獻祖、懿祖，祔玄宗、肅宗。

translations.literal: In the second year of Baoying, Xianzu and Yizu were removed to the distant line; Xuanzong and Suzong were enshrined.
translations.idiomatic: In Baoying year 2, Xianzu and Yizu were removed to the distant line; Xuanzong and Suzong were enshrined.

sentences.zh: 自是之後，常為九室矣。

translations.literal: Thereafter it was regularly nine chambers.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter it was regularly nine chambers.

sentences.zh: 代宗崩，禮儀使顏真卿議：「太祖、高祖、太宗皆不毀，而代祖元皇帝當遷。

translations.literal: When Daizong died, Ritual Commissioner Yan Zhenqing deliberated: "Grand Ancestor, Gaozu, and Taizong are not destroyed; Emperor Yuan the dynastic ancestor should be moved."
translations.idiomatic: When Daizong died, Yan Zhenqing argued: "Grand Ancestor, Gaozu, and Taizong are not destroyed; dynastic ancestor Emperor Yuan should be moved."

sentences.zh: 」於是遷元皇帝而祔代宗。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan was moved and Daizong enshrined.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan was moved and Daizong enshrined.

sentences.zh: 德宗崩，禮儀使杜黃裳議：「高宗在三昭三穆外，當遷。

translations.literal: When Dezong died, Ritual Commissioner Du Huangchang deliberated: "Gaozong is outside the three zhao and three mu and should be moved."
translations.idiomatic: When Dezong died, Du Huangchang argued: "Gaozong stands outside three zhao and three mu and should be moved."

sentences.zh: 」於是遷高宗而祔德宗，蓋以中、睿為昭穆矣。

translations.literal: Gaozong was moved and Dezong enshrined—Zhongzong and Ruizong were taken as zhao and mu.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong was moved and Dezong enshrined—Zhongzong and Ruizong serving as zhao and mu.

sentences.zh: 順宗崩，當遷中宗，而有司疑之，以謂則天革命，中宗中興之主也。

translations.literal: When Shunzong died, Zhongzong should have been moved; the responsible offices were doubtful, holding that after Wu Zetian's revolution Zhongzong was a restoration lord.
translations.idiomatic: When Shunzong died, Zhongzong should have been moved; officials hesitated, holding that after Wu Zetian's revolution Zhongzong was a restoration lord.

sentences.zh: 博士王涇、史官蔣武皆以為中宗得失在己，非漢光武、晉元帝之比，不得為中興不遷之君。

translations.literal: Academician Wang Jing and historiographer Jiang Wu all held that Zhongzong's success and failure lay in himself—not comparable to Han Guangwu or Jin Emperor Yuan—and could not be a restoration lord not moved.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jing and Jiang Wu held Zhongzong's success and failure were his own—not comparable to Guangwu or Jin Yuan—and he could not be an unmoved restoration lord.

sentences.zh: 由是遷中宗而祔順宗。

translations.literal: Zhongzong was moved and Shunzong enshrined.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongzong was moved and Shunzong enshrined.

sentences.zh: 自憲宗、穆宗、敬宗、文宗四世祔廟，睿、玄、肅、代以次遷。

translations.literal: From Xianzong, Muzong, Jingzong, and Wenzong four generations were enshrined; Ruizong, Xuanzong, Suzong, and Daizong were moved in turn.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzong, Muzong, Jingzong, and Wenzong were enshrined; Ruizong, Xuanzong, Suzong, and Daizong moved in turn.

sentences.zh: 至武宗崩，德宗以次當遷，而於世次為高祖，禮官始覺其非，以謂兄弟不相為後，不得為昭穆，乃議復祔代宗。

translations.literal: When Wuzong died, Dezong and below should have been moved; in generation sequence he was Gaozu; ritual officers first perceived the error, holding brothers do not succeed one another and cannot be zhao and mu—deliberation arose to re-enshrine Daizong.
translations.idiomatic: When Wuzong died, Dezong and below should have moved; by generation he was Gaozu; ritual officers first saw the error—brothers do not succeed one another and cannot be zhao and mu—and debated re-enshrining Daizong.

sentences.zh: 而議者言：「已祧之主不得復入太廟。

translations.literal: Deliberators said: "Lords already removed to the distant line cannot re-enter the Grand Temple."
translations.idiomatic: Critics said: "Lords already removed to the distant line cannot re-enter the Grand Temple."

sentences.zh: 」禮官曰：「昔晉元、明之世，已遷豫章、潁川，後皆復祔，此故事也。

translations.literal: Ritual officers said: "In Jin under Yuan and Ming, Yuzhang and Yingchuan had been moved yet all were later re-enshrined—this is precedent."
translations.idiomatic: Ritual officers cited Jin under Yuan and Ming, when Yuzhang and Yingchuan were moved yet later re-enshrined—precedent.

sentences.zh: 」議者又言：「廟室有定數，而無後之主當置別廟。

translations.literal: Deliberators also said: "Temple chambers have fixed numbers; lords without heirs should be placed in separate temples."
translations.idiomatic: Critics also said: "Temple chambers have fixed numbers; lords without heirs need separate temples."

sentences.zh: 」禮官曰：「晉武帝時，景、文同廟，廟雖六代，其實七主。

translations.literal: Ritual officers said: "Under Jin Emperor Wu, Jing and Wen shared a temple—though six generations in name, actually seven lords.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual officers cited Jin Emperor Wu, when Jing and Wen shared a temple—six generations in name, seven lords in fact.

sentences.zh: 至元帝、明帝，廟皆十室，故賀循曰：『廟以容主為限，而無常數也。

translations.literal: Under Yuan and Ming, temples all had ten chambers; hence He Xun said: 'Temples are limited by capacity for tablets, not by fixed number.'
translations.idiomatic: Under Yuan and Ming, temples had ten chambers; He Xun said: 'Temples are limited by capacity for tablets, not by fixed number.'"

sentences.zh: 』」於是復祔代宗，而以敬宗、文宗、武宗同為一代。

translations.literal: Daizong was re-enshrined, and Jingzong, Wenzong, and Wuzong were taken as one generation.
translations.idiomatic: Daizong was re-enshrined, and Jingzong, Wenzong, and Wuzong were counted as one generation.

sentences.zh: 初，玄宗之復祔獻祖也，詔曰：「使親而不盡，遠而不祧。

translations.literal: At first when Xuanzong re-enshrined Xianzu, the edict said: "Let intimacy not be exhausted, remoteness not cut off."
translations.idiomatic: When Xuanzong re-enshrined Xianzu, the edict said: "Let intimacy not be exhausted, remoteness not cut off."

sentences.zh: 」蓋其率意而言爾，非本於禮也。

translations.literal: That was spoken arbitrarily, not rooted in ritual.
translations.idiomatic: That was spoken arbitrarily, not rooted in ritual.

sentences.zh: 而後之為說者，乃遷就其事，以謂三昭三穆與太祖祖功宗德三廟不遷為九廟者，周制也。

translations.literal: Later theorists accommodated the affair, holding that three zhao and three mu with Grand Ancestor, zu honoring merit and zong honoring virtue three temples not moved for nine temples was Zhou institution.
translations.idiomatic: Later theorists accommodated the affair, holding nine temples—three zhao and three mu plus Grand Ancestor and unmoved zu and zong—to be Zhou institution.

sentences.zh: 及敬、文、武三宗為一代，故終唐之世，常為九代十一室焉。

translations.literal: With Jing, Wen, and Wu three houses as one generation, through the Tang it was regularly nine generations and eleven chambers.
translations.idiomatic: With Jing, Wen, and Wu as one generation, through the Tang it was regularly nine generations and eleven chambers.

sentences.zh: 開元五年，太廟四室壞，奉其神主于太極殿，天子素服避正殿，輟朝三日。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Kaiyuan, four Grand Temple chambers collapsed; spirit tablets were placed in the Hall of Supreme Ultimate; the Son of Heaven wore plain dress and avoided the main hall, suspending court for three days.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyuan year 5, four Grand Temple chambers collapsed; tablets were placed in the Hall of Supreme Ultimate; the emperor wore plain dress, avoided the main hall, and suspended court three days.

sentences.zh: 時將行幸東都，遂謁神主于太極殿而後行。

translations.literal: About to travel to the eastern capital, he paid respects to the tablets in the Hall of Supreme Ultimate before departing.
translations.idiomatic: About to travel east, he paid respects to the tablets in the Hall of Supreme Ultimate before departing.

sentences.zh: 安祿山之亂，宗廟為賊所焚，肅宗復京師，設次光順門外，嚮廟而哭，輟朝三日。

translations.literal: In An Lushan's rebellion the ancestral temple was burned by rebels; Suzong recovered the capital, set a station outside Guangshun Gate, faced the temple and wept, and suspended court three days.
translations.idiomatic: In An Lushan's rebellion the temple was burned; Suzong recovered the capital, set a station outside Guangshun Gate, faced the temple and wept, and suspended court three days.

sentences.zh: 其後黃巢陷京師，焚毀宗廟，而僖宗出奔，神主法物從行，皆為賊所掠。

translations.literal: Later Huang Chao took the capital and burned the ancestral temple; Xizong fled; spirit tablets and ritual objects traveled with him—all plundered by rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Later Huang Chao burned the temple; Xizong fled with tablets and ritual objects—all plundered by rebels.

sentences.zh: 巢敗，復京師，素服哭于廟而後入。

translations.literal: When Chao was defeated and the capital recovered, the emperor wore plain dress, wept at the temple, then entered.
translations.idiomatic: When Chao fell and the capital was recovered, the emperor wore plain dress, wept at the temple, then entered.

sentences.zh: 初，唐建東、西二都，而東都無廟。

translations.literal: At first Tang established eastern and western capitals, but the eastern capital had no temple.
translations.idiomatic: At first Tang had eastern and western capitals, but the eastern capital had no temple.

sentences.zh: 則天皇后僭號稱周，立周七廟于東都以祀武氏，改西京唐太廟為享德廟。

translations.literal: Empress Wu usurped as Zhou, established Zhou's seven temples at the eastern capital to worship the Wu clan, and changed the western capital's Tang Grand Temple to the Temple of Enjoyed Virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu usurped as Zhou, built Zhou's seven temples at the eastern capital for the Wu clan, and renamed the western capital's Tang Grand Temple Temple of Enjoyed Virtue.

sentences.zh: 神龍元年，中宗復位，遷武氏廟主于西京，為崇尊廟，而以東都武氏故廟為唐太廟，祔光皇帝以下七室而親享焉。

translations.literal: In Shenlong year 1 Zhongzong was restored; Wu clan tablets were moved to the western capital as the Temple of Honored Reverence; the eastern capital's former Wu temple became the Tang Grand Temple, enshrining from Emperor Guang seven chambers with the emperor personally offering.
translations.idiomatic: In Shenlong year 1 Zhongzong was restored; Wu tablets moved west as Temple of Honored Reverence; the eastern Wu temple became the Tang Grand Temple, enshrining from Emperor Guang seven chambers with personal imperial offerings.

sentences.zh: 由是東西二都皆有廟，歲時並享。

translations.literal: Hence both capitals had temples with seasonal joint offerings.
translations.idiomatic: Hence both capitals had temples with joint seasonal offerings.

sentences.zh: 其後安祿山陷兩京，宗廟皆焚毀。

translations.literal: Later An Lushan took both capitals and the ancestral temples were all burned.
translations.idiomatic: Later An Lushan took both capitals and burned the temples.

sentences.zh: 肅宗即位，西都建廟作主，而東都太廟毀為軍營，九室神主亡失，至大曆中，始於人間得之，寓于太微宮，不復祔享。

translations.literal: When Suzong took the throne, the western capital built a temple and tablets; the eastern Grand Temple was destroyed for barracks, nine chambers' tablets lost—only in the Dali era recovered among the people, lodged at Taiwei Palace, never re-enshrined.
translations.idiomatic: Suzong built the western temple; the eastern Grand Temple became barracks, nine chambers' tablets lost—recovered in the Dali era, lodged at Taiwei Palace, never re-enshrined.

sentences.zh: 自建中至于會昌，議者不一，或以為：「東西二京宜皆有廟，而舊主當瘞，虛其廟以俟，巡幸則載主而行。

translations.literal: From Jianzhong to Huichang deliberators differed; some held: "Both capitals should have temples; old tablets should be buried, the temple left vacant to await; on imperial tours tablets should be carried."
translations.idiomatic: From Jianzhong to Huichang debate continued; some held both capitals should have temples, old tablets buried, the temple left vacant, tablets carried on tours.

sentences.zh: 」或謂：「宜藏其神主于夾室。

translations.literal: Others said tablets should be stored in side chambers.
translations.idiomatic: Others said tablets should be stored in side chambers.

sentences.zh: 」或曰：「周豐、洛有廟者，因遷都乃立廟爾，今東都不因遷而立廟，非也。

translations.literal: Others said Zhou's Feng and Luo had temples because of relocation—today's eastern capital was not established by relocation, which is wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Others said Zhou's Feng and Luo had temples only because of relocation—the eastern capital was not founded by relocation, which is wrong.

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「古者載主以行者，惟新遷一室之主爾，未有載羣廟之主者也。

translations.literal: Others said in antiquity carrying tablets on journeys was only for a newly moved single chamber's lord—never carrying the whole temple's tablets.
translations.idiomatic: Others said antiquity carried tablets only for a newly moved single chamber—never a whole temple's tablets.

sentences.zh: 」至武宗時，悉廢羣議，詔有司擇日修東都廟。

translations.literal: By Wuzong's time all debates were abolished; an edict ordered the offices to choose a day to repair the eastern-capital temple.
translations.idiomatic: By Wuzong all debates were abolished; an edict ordered repair of the eastern-capital temple.

sentences.zh: 已而武宗崩，宣宗竟以太微神主祔東都廟焉。

translations.literal: Wuzong then died; Xuanzong finally enshrined the Taiwei tablets in the eastern-capital temple.
translations.idiomatic: Wuzong then died; Xuanzong enshrined the Taiwei tablets in the eastern-capital temple.

sentences.zh: 其追贈皇后、追尊皇太后、贈皇太子往往皆立別廟。

translations.literal: Posthumous honors for empresses, empress dowagers, and crown princes often each had separate temples.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumous honors for empresses, empress dowagers, and crown princes often each had separate temples.

sentences.zh: 其近於禮者，後世當求諸禮。

translations.literal: What approaches ritual—later ages should seek it in ritual.
translations.idiomatic: What approaches ritual, later ages should judge by ritual.

sentences.zh: 其不合於禮而出其私意者，蓋其制作與其論議皆不足取焉，故不著也。

translations.literal: What does not accord with ritual and issues from private intent—their constructions and debates are not worth taking; hence they are not recorded.
translations.idiomatic: What violates ritual and serves private whim—its constructions and debates are not worth recording; hence they are omitted.

sentences.zh: 宣宗已復河、湟三州七關，歸其功順宗、憲宗而加謚號。

translations.literal: Xuanzong had recovered the three prefectures and seven passes of He and Huang; he attributed the merit to Shunzong and Xianzong and added posthumous titles.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzong recovered the three prefectures and seven passes of He and Huang; he credited Shunzong and Xianzong and added posthumous titles.

sentences.zh: 博士李稠請改作神主，易書新謚。

translations.literal: Academician Li Chou requested remaking spirit tablets and changing the text for new posthumous titles.
translations.idiomatic: Academician Li Chou requested remaking spirit tablets and rewriting them for new posthumous titles.

sentences.zh: 右司郎中楊發等議，以謂：「古者已祔之主無改作，加謚追尊，非禮也，始於則天，然猶不改主易書，宜以新謚寶冊告于陵廟可也。

translations.literal: Right Bureau Director Yang Fa and others deliberated, holding: "In antiquity already enshrined tablets were not remade; adding posthumous titles and posthumous elevation is not ritual—it began under Wu Zetian, yet even then tablets were not remade or texts changed; it suffices to announce new posthumous seals at tomb and temple."
translations.idiomatic: Yang Fa and others argued: "In antiquity enshrined tablets were not remade; adding posthumous titles is not ritual—it began under Wu Zetian, yet even then tablets were not remade; new posthumous seals should be announced at tomb and temple."

sentences.zh: 」是時，宰相以謂士族之廟皆就易書，乃就舊主易書新謚焉。

translations.literal: At that time the chief ministers held that gentry clan temples all changed texts on old tablets—so old tablets were changed for new posthumous titles.
translations.idiomatic: Chief ministers noted gentry temples all rewrote old tablets—so imperial tablets were rewritten for new posthumous titles.

sentences.zh: 禘、祫，大祭也。

translations.literal: Di and xia are great sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Di and xia are great sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 祫以昭穆合食于太祖，而禘以審諦其尊卑，此祫、禘之義，而為禮者失之，至於年數不同，祖、宗失位，而議者莫知所從。

translations.literal: Xia joins zhao and mu in joint feasting at the Grand Ancestor; di scrutinizes honor and baseness—this is the meaning of xia and di; yet ritualists lost it until year-counts differed and zu and zong lost position, and deliberators knew not which to follow.
translations.idiomatic: Xia joins zhao and mu at the Grand Ancestor; di scrutinizes rank—this is their meaning; yet ritualists lost it until year-counts diverged and zu and zong lost place, and debaters knew not which view to follow.

sentences.zh: 禮曰：「三年一祫，五年一禘。

translations.literal: The Rites say: "Xia every three years, di every five years."
translations.idiomatic: The Rites say: "Xia every three years, di every five years."

sentences.zh: 」傳曰：「五年再殷祭。

translations.literal: The Commentary says: "Every five years, two full sacrifices."
translations.idiomatic: The Commentary says: "Every five years, two full sacrifices."

sentences.zh: 」高宗上元三年十月當祫，而有司疑其年數。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of Gaozong's third Shangyuan year xia was due; the responsible offices doubted the year-count.
translations.idiomatic: In Gaozong's Shangyuan year 3, tenth month, xia was due; officials doubted the year-count.

sentences.zh: 太學博士史玄璨等議，以為：「新君喪畢而祫，明年而禘。

translations.literal: University Academician Shi Xuanzan and others deliberated, holding: "After the new lord's mourning ends comes xia; the next year di.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Xuanzan and others argued: "After the new ruler's mourning ends comes xia; the next year di."

sentences.zh: 自是之後，五年而再祭。

translations.literal: Thereafter every five years two sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter sacrifices came every five years.

sentences.zh: 蓋後禘去前禘五年，而祫常在禘後三年，禘常在祫後二年。

translations.literal: The later di is five years from the former di; xia is regularly three years after di; di regularly two years after xia.
translations.idiomatic: Later di falls five years after earlier di; xia regularly three years after di; di two years after xia.

sentences.zh: 魯宣公八年禘僖公，蓋二年喪畢而祫，明年而禘，至八年而再禘。

translations.literal: In Lu Duke Xuan's eighth year di to Duke Xi—mourning ended in the second year and xia came; the next year di; by the eighth year di again.
translations.idiomatic: Lu in Duke Xuan year 8 di to Duke Xi—mourning ended in year 2 with xia; di the next year; di again by year 8.

sentences.zh: 昭公二十年禘，至二十五年又禘，此可知也。

translations.literal: Duke Zhao's twentieth year di; by the twenty-fifth year di again—this can be known.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Zhao year 20 di; di again by year 25—this shows the pattern.

sentences.zh: 」議者以玄璨等言有經據，遂從之。

translations.literal: Deliberators held Shi Xuanzan and others' words had canonical basis and followed them.
translations.idiomatic: Debaters found Shi Xuanzan's argument canonical and followed it.

sentences.zh: 睿宗崩，開元六年喪畢而祫，明年而禘。

translations.literal: When Ruizong died, in the sixth year of Kaiyuan mourning ended and xia came; the next year di.
translations.idiomatic: When Ruizong died, Kaiyuan year 6 mourning ended and xia came; di the next year.

sentences.zh: 自是之後，祫、禘各自以年，不相通數。

translations.literal: Thereafter xia and di each kept its own year-count, not communicating numbers.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter xia and di each kept separate year-counts.

sentences.zh: 凡七祫五禘，至二十七年，禘、祫並在一歲，有司覺其非，乃議以為一禘一祫，五年再殷，宜通數。

translations.literal: Seven xia and five di in all; by the twenty-seventh year di and xia fell in one year; the offices perceived the error and deliberated that one di and one xia, two full sacrifices in five years, should communicate numbers.
translations.idiomatic: Seven xia and five di in all; by year 27 di and xia fell in one year; officials saw the error and argued one di and one xia in five years should share a single count.

sentences.zh: 而禘後置祫，歲數遠近，二說不同。

translations.literal: Yet whether xia follows di and the distance in years—two theories differ.
translations.idiomatic: Yet whether xia follows di and the interval in years—two theories differed.

sentences.zh: 鄭玄用高堂隆先三而後二，徐邈先二後三。

translations.literal: Zheng Xuan used Gao Tanglong's three-then-two; Xu Miao two-then-three.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan followed Gao Tanglong's three-then-two; Xu Miao two-then-three.

sentences.zh: 而邈以謂二禘相去為月六十，中分三十，置一祫焉。

translations.literal: Miao held two di sixty months apart, split thirty, and placed one xia between.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Miao held two di sixty months apart, split the interval in half, and placed one xia between.

sentences.zh: 此最為得，遂用其說。

translations.literal: This was most correct and his theory was adopted.
translations.idiomatic: This was judged most correct and adopted.

sentences.zh: 由是一禘一祫，在五年之間，合於再殷之義，而置祫先後，則不同焉。

translations.literal: Hence one di and one xia within five years accorded with two full sacrifices, while placement of xia before or after differed.
translations.idiomatic: Hence one di and one xia within five years matched two full sacrifices, while xia's placement before or after di differed.

sentences.zh: 禮，禘、祫，太祖位于西而東向，其子孫列為昭穆，昭南向而穆北向。

translations.literal: In ritual, at di and xia the Grand Ancestor's seat is west facing east; descendants are arrayed as zhao and mu—zhao south-facing, mu north-facing.
translations.idiomatic: At di and xia the Grand Ancestor sits west facing east; descendants array as zhao and mu—zhao south-facing, mu north-facing.

sentences.zh: 雖已毀廟之主，皆出而序于昭穆。

translations.literal: Even lords of destroyed temples all come forth and are sequenced in zhao and mu.
translations.idiomatic: Even lords of destroyed temples come forth and take place in zhao and mu.

sentences.zh: 殷、周之興，太祖世遠，而羣廟之主皆出其後，故其禮易明。

translations.literal: Yin and Zhou's rise: the Grand Ancestor's generation was remote and host temples' lords all issued after him—hence the rite was easy to clarify.
translations.idiomatic: In Yin and Zhou's rise the Grand Ancestor stood generations remote and all moved lords descended after him—hence the rite was clear.

sentences.zh: 漢、魏以來，其興也暴，又其上世微，故創國之君為太祖而世近，毀廟之主皆在太祖之上，於是禘、祫不得如古。

translations.literal: From Han and Wei, rise was sudden and upper generations obscure; the founding lord became Grand Ancestor yet generation was near, and destroyed temples' lords were all above the Grand Ancestor—thus di and xia could not match antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: From Han and Wei rise was sudden and forebears obscure; the founding lord became Grand Ancestor yet stood near in generation, destroyed lords all above him—di and xia could not match antiquity.

sentences.zh: 而漢、魏之制，太祖而上，毀廟之主皆不合食。

translations.literal: In Han and Wei institution, lords above the Grand Ancestor did not jointly feast.
translations.idiomatic: Under Han and Wei, lords above the Grand Ancestor did not join joint feasting.

sentences.zh: 唐興，以景皇帝為太祖，而世近在三昭三穆之內，至祫、禘，乃虛東向之位，而太祖與羣廟列於昭穆。

translations.literal: Tang's rise took Emperor Jing as Grand Ancestor, generation near within three zhao and three mu; at xia and di the east-facing seat was left vacant and the Grand Ancestor was arrayed with host temples in zhao and mu.
translations.idiomatic: Tang took Emperor Jing as Grand Ancestor, near within three zhao and three mu; at xia and di the east-facing seat was left vacant and the Grand Ancestor stood among zhao and mu.

sentences.zh: 代宗即位，祔玄宗、肅宗，而遷獻祖、懿祖于夾室。

translations.literal: When Daizong took the throne, Xuanzong and Suzong were enshrined; Xianzu and Yizu moved to side chambers.
translations.idiomatic: When Daizong took the throne, Xuanzong and Suzong were enshrined; Xianzu and Yizu moved to side chambers.

sentences.zh: 於是太祖居第一室，禘、祫得正其位而東向，而獻、懿不合食。
