translations.literal: The Grand Ancestor then occupied the first chamber; di and xia could set his seat east-facing, while Xian and Yi did not jointly feast.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Ancestor occupied the first chamber; di and xia could seat him east-facing, while Xian and Yi did not join feasting.

sentences.zh: 建中二年，太學博士陳京請為獻祖、懿祖立別廟，至禘、祫則享。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianzhong, University Academician Chen Jing requested separate temples for Xianzu and Yizu, offering at di and xia.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianzhong year 2, Chen Jing requested separate temples for Xianzu and Yizu, offering at di and xia.

sentences.zh: 禮儀使顏真卿議曰：「太祖景皇帝居百代不遷之尊，而禘、祫之時，暫居昭穆，屈己以奉祖宗可也。

translations.literal: Ritual Commissioner Yan Zhenqing deliberated: "Grand Ancestor Emperor Jing holds honor unmoved for a hundred generations; at di and xia temporarily standing in zhao and mu, humbling himself to serve ancestors—is acceptable."
translations.idiomatic: Yan Zhenqing argued: "Grand Ancestor Emperor Jing holds unmoved honor; temporarily standing in zhao and mu at di and xia to serve ancestors is acceptable."

sentences.zh: 」乃引晉蔡謨議，以獻祖居東向，而懿祖、太祖以下左右為昭穆。

translations.literal: He cited Jin Cai Mo's deliberation: Xianzu east-facing, Yizu and Grand Ancestor below left and right as zhao and mu.
translations.idiomatic: He cited Jin Cai Mo: Xianzu east-facing, Yizu and Grand Ancestor below as zhao and mu.

sentences.zh: 由是議者紛然。

translations.literal: Deliberators grew tangled.
translations.idiomatic: Debate grew tangled.

sentences.zh: 貞元十七年，太常卿裴郁議，以太祖百代不遷，獻、懿二祖親盡廟遷而居東向，非是。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year of Zhenyuan, Director of Imperial Sacrifices Pei Yu deliberated that the Grand Ancestor, unmoved for a hundred generations, with Xian and Yi exhausted in intimacy, temples moved yet seated east-facing—was wrong.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenyuan year 17, Pei Yu argued the unmoved Grand Ancestor with Xian and Yi, intimacy exhausted and temples moved, seated east-facing—was wrong.

sentences.zh: 請下百寮議。

translations.literal: Request sending down to the hundred officials for deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: He requested referral to all officials.

sentences.zh: 工部郎中張薦等議與真卿同。

translations.literal: Bureau Director Zhang Jian and others agreed with Zhenqing.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jian and others agreed with Yan Zhenqing.

sentences.zh: 太子左庶子李嶸等七人曰：「真卿所用，晉蔡謨之議也。

translations.literal: Left Mentor of the Heir Li Rong and seven others said: "What Zhenqing used was Jin Cai Mo's deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: Li Rong and seven others said: "Zhenqing followed Jin Cai Mo.

sentences.zh: 謨為『禹不先鯀』之說，雖有其言，當時不用。

translations.literal: Mo made the 'Yu did not place Gun first' argument—though he said it, it was not used at the time.
translations.idiomatic: Mo argued 'Yu did not place Gun first'—though recorded, it was not adopted.

sentences.zh: 獻、懿二祖宜藏夾室，以合祭法『遠廟為祧，而壇、墠有禱則祭，無禱則止』之義。

translations.literal: Xian and Yi should be stored in side chambers, accordant with the Canon of Sacrifices: 'Remote temples become tiao; at altars and mounds sacrifice when there is prayer, stop when none.'"
translations.idiomatic: Xian and Yi should rest in side chambers, per the Canon: 'Remote temples become tiao; at altars sacrifice when prayed, stop when not.'"

sentences.zh: 」吏部郎中柳冕等十二人曰：「周禮有先公之祧，遷祖藏於后稷之廟，其周未受命之祧乎？

translations.literal: Bureau Director Liu Mian and twelve others said: "The Zhou Rites have the former duke's tiao, moved ancestors stored in Hou Ji's temple—is that Zhou before receiving the Mandate's tiao?
translations.idiomatic: Liu Mian and twelve others said: "The Zhou Rites have the former duke's tiao, moved ancestors stored in Hou Ji's temple—is that Zhou before the Mandate?"

sentences.zh: 又有先王之祧，其遷主藏於文、武之廟，其周已受命之祧乎？

translations.literal: There is also the former king's tiao, moved lords stored in Wen and Wu's temple—is that Zhou after receiving the Mandate's tiao?
translations.idiomatic: There is the former king's tiao, moved lords stored in Wen and Wu's temple—is that after the Mandate?"

sentences.zh: 今獻祖、懿祖，猶周先公也，請築別廟以居之。

translations.literal: Now Xianzu and Yizu are like Zhou's former dukes—request building separate temples to house them."
translations.idiomatic: Xianzu and Yizu are like Zhou's former dukes—build separate temples for them."

sentences.zh: 」司勳員外郎裴樞曰：「建石室於寢園以藏神主，至禘、祫之歲則祭之。

translations.literal: Commissioner Pei Shu said: "Build stone chambers in the tomb park to store tablets; offer at di and xia years."
translations.idiomatic: Pei Shu said: "Build stone chambers in the tomb park for tablets; offer in di and xia years."

sentences.zh: 」考功員外郎陳京、同官縣尉仲子陵皆曰：「遷神主於德明、興聖廟。

translations.literal: Commissioner Chen Jing and Tongguan County Lieutenant Zhong Ziling both said: "Move tablets to the Deming and Xingsheng temples."
translations.idiomatic: Chen Jing and Zhong Ziling both said: "Move tablets to the Deming and Xingsheng temples."

sentences.zh: 」京兆少尹韋武曰：「祫則獻祖東向，禘則太祖東向。

translations.literal: Capital Intendant Wei Wu said: "At xia Xianzu east-facing; at di the Grand Ancestor east-facing."
translations.idiomatic: Wei Wu said: "At xia Xianzu faces east; at di the Grand Ancestor faces east."

sentences.zh: 」十一年，左司郎中陸淳曰：「議者多矣，不過三而已。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, Left Bureau Director Lu Chun said: "Deliberations are many—no more than three.
translations.idiomatic: In year 11, Lu Chun said: "Debates boil down to three views."

sentences.zh: 一曰復太祖之正位，二曰並列昭穆而虛東向，三曰祫則獻祖，禘則太祖，迭居東向。

translations.literal: First, restore the Grand Ancestor's proper seat; second, array zhao and mu jointly and leave east vacant; third, at xia Xianzu, at di the Grand Ancestor, alternately east-facing.
translations.idiomatic: First restore the Grand Ancestor's seat; second array zhao and mu with east vacant; third alternate Xianzu at xia and Grand Ancestor at di east-facing.

sentences.zh: 而復正太祖之位為是。

translations.literal: Restoring the Grand Ancestor's proper seat is correct.
translations.idiomatic: Restoring the Grand Ancestor's proper seat is correct.

sentences.zh: 然太祖復位，則獻、懿之主宜有所歸。

translations.literal: Yet if the Grand Ancestor is restored, Xian and Yi's tablets need a home.
translations.idiomatic: Yet restoring the Grand Ancestor requires a home for Xian and Yi's tablets.

sentences.zh: 一曰藏諸夾室，二曰置之別廟，三曰遷于園寢，四曰祔於興聖。

translations.literal: First, store in side chambers; second, place in separate temples; third, move to tomb park; fourth, enshrine at Xingsheng.
translations.idiomatic: Options: side chambers; separate temples; tomb park; enshrine at Xingsheng.

sentences.zh: 然而藏諸夾室，則無饗獻之期；

translations.literal: Yet storing in side chambers has no term for offering;
translations.idiomatic: Storing in side chambers offers no feast schedule;

sentences.zh: 置之別廟，則非禮經之文；

translations.literal: placing in separate temples lacks canonical text;
translations.idiomatic: separate temples lack canonical text;

sentences.zh: 遷于寢園，則亂宗廟之儀。

translations.literal: moving to the tomb park disrupts ancestral temple protocol.
translations.idiomatic: tomb park storage disrupts temple protocol.

sentences.zh: 唯祔于興聖為是。

translations.literal: Only enshrining at Xingsheng is correct."
translations.idiomatic: Only enshrining at Xingsheng is correct."

sentences.zh: 」至十九年，左僕射姚南仲等獻議五十七封，付都省集議。

translations.literal: By the nineteenth year Left Vice Director Yao Nanzhong and others submitted fifty-seven memorials for collective deliberation at the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: By year 19 Yao Nanzhong submitted fifty-seven memorials for collective deliberation.

sentences.zh: 戶部尚書王紹等五十五人請遷懿祖祔興聖廟，議遂定，由是太祖始復東向之位。

translations.literal: Minister of Revenue Wang Shao and fifty-five others requested moving Yizu to enshrine at Xingsheng; deliberation was fixed—thus the Grand Ancestor at last regained the east-facing seat.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shao and fifty-five others moved Yizu to Xingsheng; debate ended—the Grand Ancestor regained the east-facing seat.

sentences.zh: 若諸臣之享其親，廟室、服器之數，視其品。

translations.literal: As for ministers offering to their kin, temple chambers and ritual vessels depend on rank.
translations.idiomatic: For ministers honoring kin, temple chambers and vessels depend on rank.

sentences.zh: 開元十二年著令，一品、二品四廟，三品三廟，五品二廟，嫡士一廟，庶人祭於寢。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Kaiyuan regulations were issued: first and second rank four temples, third rank three, fifth rank two, legitimate gentry one, commoners sacrifice in the sleeping chamber.
translations.idiomatic: Kaiyuan year 12 regulations: ranks 1–2 four temples, rank 3 three, rank 5 two, legitimate gentry one, commoners sacrifice in the chamber.

sentences.zh: 及定禮，二品以上四廟，三品三廟，三品以上不須爵者亦四廟，四廟有始封為五廟，四品、五品有兼爵亦三廟，六品以下達于庶人，祭於寢。

translations.literal: When rites were fixed: second rank and above four temples, third rank three; third rank and above without ennoblement also four; four temples with original enfeoffment make five; ranks 4–5 with concurrent ennoblement also three; sixth rank and below down to commoners sacrifice in the chamber.
translations.idiomatic: When rites were fixed: rank 2+ four temples, rank 3 three; rank 3+ without title also four; original enfeoffment makes five; ranks 4–5 with title three; rank 6 down to commoners sacrifice in the chamber.

sentences.zh: 天寶十載，京官正員四品清望及四品、五品清官，聽立廟，勿限兼爵。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Tianbao, capital officials of regular fourth rank in clear expectation and fourth- and fifth-rank clear offices were permitted temples without limit on concurrent titles.
translations.idiomatic: Tianbao year 10: capital officials of regular fourth rank in clear expectation and fourth- and fifth-rank clear offices could build temples regardless of concurrent titles.

sentences.zh: 雖品及而建廟未逮，亦聽寢祭。

translations.literal: Though rank qualified yet temple not yet built, chamber sacrifice was still permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Though rank qualified before a temple was built, chamber sacrifice was permitted.

sentences.zh: 廟之制，三品以上九架，廈兩旁。

translations.literal: Temple regulations: third rank and above nine bays with side galleries.
translations.idiomatic: Temple design: rank 3+ nine bays with side galleries.

sentences.zh: 三廟者五間，中為三室，左右廈一間，前後虛之，無重栱、藻井。

translations.literal: Three-temple holders five bays, center three chambers, side galleries one bay each, void front and rear, no bracket sets or caisson ceilings.
translations.idiomatic: Three-temple holders: five bays, three central chambers, one-bay side galleries, void front and rear, no bracket sets or caisson ceilings.

sentences.zh: 室皆為石室一，於西墉三之一近南，距地四尺，容二主。

translations.literal: Each chamber one stone chamber on the western wall one-third from the south, four feet from ground, holding two tablets.
translations.idiomatic: Each chamber: one stone niche on the western wall one-third from the south, four feet high, holding two tablets.

sentences.zh: 廟垣周之，為南門、東門，門屋三室，而上間以廟，增建神廚於廟東之少南，齋院於東門之外少北，制勿逾於廟。

translations.literal: Temple walls surround it with south and east gates, gate buildings three bays, upper bay as temple; add spirit kitchen southeast of temple, fasting compound north of east gate—scale not exceeding the temple.
translations.idiomatic: Walls with south and east gates, three-bay gate buildings; spirit kitchen southeast, fasting compound north of east gate—nothing larger than the temple.

sentences.zh: 三品以上有神主，五品以上有几筵。

translations.literal: Third rank and above have spirit tablets; fifth rank and above have offering mats.
translations.idiomatic: Rank 3+ have spirit tablets; rank 5+ have offering mats.

sentences.zh: 牲以少牢，羊、豕一，六品以下特豚，不以祖禰貴賤，皆子孫之牲。

translations.literal: Victims are shao lao—one sheep and one pig; sixth rank and below single suckling pig; regardless of ancestor rank, all are descendants' victims.
translations.idiomatic: Victims: shao lao—one sheep and one pig; rank 6 and below a single suckling pig; all descendants' offerings regardless of ancestor rank.

sentences.zh: 牲闕，代以野獸。

translations.literal: If victims are lacking, wild beasts substitute.
translations.idiomatic: If victims are lacking, wild game substitutes.

sentences.zh: 五品以上室異牲，六品以下共牲。

translations.literal: Fifth rank and above separate victims per chamber; sixth rank and below share.
translations.idiomatic: Rank 5+ separate victims per chamber; rank 6 and below share.

sentences.zh: 二品以上室以籩豆十，三品以八，四品、五品以六。

translations.literal: Second rank and above ten baskets and stands per chamber; third rank eight; fourth and fifth six.
translations.idiomatic: Rank 2+ ten baskets and stands per chamber; rank 3 eight; ranks 4–5 six.

sentences.zh: 五品以上室皆簠二、簋二、㽅二、鈃二、俎三、尊二、罍二、勺二、爵六、盤一、坫一、篚一、牙盤胙俎一。

translations.literal: Fifth rank and above per chamber: two grain trays, two grain bowls, two ladled cups, two bells, three stands, two wine jars, two urns, two ladles, six goblets, one basin, one mound, one basket, one tooth-tray sacrificial stand.
translations.idiomatic: Rank 5+ per chamber: two grain trays, two bowls, two cups, two bells, three stands, two jars, two urns, two ladles, six goblets, one basin, one mound, one basket, one sacrificial stand.

sentences.zh: 祭服，三品以上玄冕，五品以上爵弁，六品以下進賢冠，各以其服。

translations.literal: Sacrificial dress: third rank and above dark coronet; fifth rank and above cap of nobility; sixth rank and below advancement-worthy cap, each in his regular dress.
translations.idiomatic: Sacrificial dress: rank 3+ dark coronet; rank 5+ cap of nobility; rank 6 and below advancement-worthy cap in regular dress.

sentences.zh: 凡祔皆給休五日，時享皆四日。

translations.literal: All enshrinements grant five days' rest; seasonal offerings four days.
translations.idiomatic: Enshrinement grants five days' rest; seasonal offerings four.

sentences.zh: 散齋二日於正寢，致齋一日於廟，子孫陪者齋一宿於家。

translations.literal: Two days dispersed fasting in the main residence, one day concentrated fasting at the temple; accompanying descendants fast one night at home.
translations.idiomatic: Two days dispersed fasting at home, one day at the temple; accompanying descendants fast one night at home.

sentences.zh: 始廟則署主而祔，後喪闋乃祔，喪二十八月上旬卜而祔，始神事之矣。

translations.literal: When first establishing a temple, inscribe the tablet then enshrine; after mourning ends then enshrine; in the upper ten days of the twenty-eighth month of mourning, divine and enshrine—then spirit affairs begin.
translations.idiomatic: New temples: inscribe the tablet then enshrine; after mourning ends; divine in the upper ten days of month 28 of mourning—then spirit rites begin.

sentences.zh: 王公之主載以輅，夫人之主以翟車，其餘皆以輿。

translations.literal: Dukes and marquises' tablets are carried on chariots, ladies' on pheasant carts, others on litters.
translations.idiomatic: Dukes' tablets ride chariots, ladies' pheasant carts, others litters.

sentences.zh: 天子以四孟、臘享太廟，諸臣避之，祭仲而不臘。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven offers at the Grand Temple on the four meng and la days; ministers avoid them—sacrificing to Zhong but not la.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor offers at the Grand Temple on four meng and la days; ministers avoid them—sacrifice to Zhong but not la.

sentences.zh: 三歲一祫，五歲一禘。

translations.literal: Xia every three years, di every five.
translations.idiomatic: Xia every three years, di every five.

sentences.zh: 若祔、若常享、若禘祫，卜日、齋戒、省牲、視滌、濯鼎鑊，亨牲、實饌、三獻、飲福、受胙進退之數，大抵如宗廟之祀。

translations.literal: Whether enshrining, seasonal offering, or di and xia—the numbers for divining days, fasting, inspecting victims, viewing wash-water, scouring cauldrons, cooking victims, filling offerings, three presentations, drinking blessing, receiving sacrificial flesh, advance and retreat—are mostly like ancestral temple sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Enshrining, seasonal offerings, di and xia—divining days, fasting, inspecting victims, wash-water, cauldrons, cooking, offerings, three presentations, blessing wine, sacrificial flesh, advance and retreat—mostly follow Grand Temple protocol.

sentences.zh: 以國官亞、終獻，無則以親賓，以子弟。

translations.literal: State officials as secondary and final presenters; if none, kin guests or younger kinsmen.
translations.idiomatic: State officials serve as secondary and final presenters; if none, kin guests or younger kinsmen.

sentences.zh: 其後不卜日，而筮用亥。

translations.literal: Later days were not divined; divination used the hai day.
translations.idiomatic: Later they ceased divining days; divination used the hai day.

sentences.zh: 祭寢者，春、秋以分，冬、夏以至日。

translations.literal: Chamber sacrifice: spring and autumn at the equinoxes, winter and summer at the solstices.
translations.idiomatic: Chamber sacrifice: spring and autumn at equinoxes, winter and summer at solstices.

sentences.zh: 若祭春分，則廢元日。

translations.literal: If sacrificing at spring equinox, the first-of-year day is canceled.
translations.idiomatic: If sacrificing at spring equinox, New Year's day is canceled.

sentences.zh: 然元正，歲之始，冬至，陽之復，二節最重。

translations.literal: Yet New Year's day begins the year; winter solstice restores yang—these two nodes weigh heaviest.
translations.idiomatic: Yet New Year's begins the year and winter solstice restores yang—the two weightiest nodes.

sentences.zh: 祭不欲數，乃廢春分，通為四。

translations.literal: Sacrifice should not be frequent—spring equinox was canceled, totaling four.
translations.idiomatic: Sacrifice should not be too frequent—spring equinox was dropped, leaving four.

sentences.zh: 祠器以烏漆，差小常制。

translations.literal: Temple vessels black lacquer, somewhat smaller than regular measure.
translations.idiomatic: Temple vessels black lacquer, somewhat smaller than standard measure.

sentences.zh: 祭服以進賢冠，主婦花釵禮衣，後或改衣冠從公服，無則常服。

translations.literal: Sacrificial dress advancement-worthy cap; mistress flower hairpin and ritual robe; later sometimes changed to follow official dress; if none, regular dress.
translations.idiomatic: Sacrificial dress: advancement-worthy cap; mistress flower pin and ritual robe; later sometimes official dress; otherwise regular dress.

sentences.zh: 凡祭之在廟、在寢，既畢，皆親賓子孫慰，主人以常服見。

translations.literal: All sacrifices in temple or chamber, when finished, kin guests and descendants console; the host receives them in regular dress.
translations.idiomatic: When temple or chamber sacrifice ends, kin and descendants console; the host receives them in regular dress.

sentences.zh: 若宗子有故，庶子攝祭，則祝曰：「孝子某使介子某執其常事。

translations.literal: If the lineage heir has cause, a lesser son conducts sacrifice—the invoker says: "Filial son So-and-so has lesser son So-and-so perform the regular affairs."
translations.idiomatic: If the lineage heir is absent, a lesser son conducts sacrifice—the invoker says: "Filial son X has lesser son Y perform the regular rites."

sentences.zh: 」通祭三代，而宗子卑，則以上牲祭宗子家，祝曰：「孝子某為其介子某薦其常事。

translations.literal: When offering through three generations and the lineage heir is low in standing, the superior victim is offered at the lineage heir's house—the invoker says: "Filial son So-and-so offers through lesser son So-and-so the regular affairs."
translations.idiomatic: When offering across three generations and the lineage heir ranks low, the superior victim goes to his house—the invoker says: "Filial son X offers through lesser son Y the regular rites."

sentences.zh: 」庶子官尊而立廟，其主祭則以支庶封官依大宗主祭，兄陪於位。

translations.literal: When a lesser son's office is lofty and he establishes a temple, the chief sacrificer is the enfeoffed collateral official following the great lineage's sacrifice, the elder brother accompanying at the seat.
translations.idiomatic: When a lesser son's office is lofty and he builds a temple, the chief sacrificer is the enfeoffed collateral following the great lineage, the elder brother at the seat.

sentences.zh: 以廟由弟立，己不得延神也。

translations.literal: Because the temple was established by the younger brother, he himself cannot extend the spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Because the younger brother built the temple, he cannot himself host the spirit.

sentences.zh: 或兄弟分官，則各祭考妣於正寢。

translations.literal: Or when brothers hold separate offices, each sacrifices to father and mother in the main chamber.
translations.idiomatic: Or when brothers hold separate offices, each sacrifices to parents in the main chamber.

sentences.zh: 古殤及無後皆祔食於祖，無祝而不拜，設坐祖左而西向，亞獻者奠，祝乃奠之，一獻而止。

translations.literal: In antiquity premature death and the heirless all received collateral feasting at the ancestor; no invoker and no bowing; seat set left of ancestor facing west; secondary presenter sets offering, then invoker sets offering—one presentation only.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity the prematurely dead and heirless received collateral feasting at the ancestor; no invoker, no bowing; seat left of ancestor facing west; secondary presenter sets offering, invoker then sets offering—one presentation only.

sentences.zh: 其後廟制設幄，當中南向，祔坐無所施，皆祭室戶外之東而西向。

translations.literal: Later temple design set a canopy, center south-facing; collateral seats had nowhere to go—all sacrificed east of the chamber door facing west.
translations.idiomatic: Later temples set a south-facing canopy at center; collateral seats had no place—all sacrificed east of the chamber door facing west.

sentences.zh: 親伯叔之無後者祔曾祖，親昆弟及從父昆弟祔於祖，親子姪祔於禰。

translations.literal: Collateral paternal uncles without heirs enshrine at great-grandfather; full and paternal cousins at grandfather; sons and nephews at father.
translations.idiomatic: Heirless paternal uncles enshrine at great-grandfather; full and paternal cousins at grandfather; sons and nephews at father.

sentences.zh: 寢祭之位西上，祖東向而昭穆南北，則伯叔之祔者居禰下之穆位北向，昆弟、從父昆弟居祖下之昭位南向，子姪居伯叔之下穆位北向，以序尊卑。

translations.literal: Chamber sacrifice seats rank west highest; ancestor east-facing with zhao and mu north and south—collateral uncles below father in mu seat north-facing, brothers and cousins below grandfather in zhao south-facing, sons and nephews below uncles in mu north-facing, sequencing honor and baseness.
translations.idiomatic: Chamber seats rank west highest; ancestor east-facing, zhao and mu north and south—uncles below father north in mu, brothers below grandfather south in zhao, sons and nephews below uncles north in mu, by rank.

sentences.zh: 凡殤、無後，以周親及大功為斷。

translations.literal: For premature death and the heirless, the limit is close kin and great-grief mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Premature death and the heirless are limited to close kin and great-grief mourners.

sentences.zh: 古者廟於大門內，秦出寢於陵側，故王公亦建廟於墓。

translations.literal: In antiquity temples stood inside the great gate; Qin moved the sleeping chamber to the tomb side—hence dukes and marquises also built temples at the tomb.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity temples stood inside the great gate; Qin moved the sleeping chamber beside the tomb—hence nobles also built temples at the tomb.

sentences.zh: 既廟與居異，則宮中有喪而祭。

translations.literal: Once temple and residence differed, sacrifice continued when there was mourning in the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Once temple and residence were separate, sacrifice could continue despite palace mourning.

sentences.zh: 三年之喪，齊衰、大功皆廢祭；

translations.literal: In three-year mourning, qi and da mourning both suspend sacrifice;
translations.idiomatic: During three-year mourning, qi and da mourning both suspend sacrifice;

sentences.zh: 外喪，齊衰以下行之。

translations.literal: for external mourning, qi and below still apply.
translations.idiomatic: for external mourning, qi mourning and below still permit sacrifice.
